content: Manchester City captain Vincent Kompany has criticized UEFA's Financial Fair Play (FFP) regulations, arguing that they protect established clubs, not prevent teams from bankruptcy. Last year, City were fined £50million and ordered to limit their transfer spending due to FFP breaches, while rivals Manchester United were able to spend £150m despite being £400m in debt. Kompany believes FFP hampers smaller clubs' ability to challenge the established elite, stating that City's success is in part due to their owners' investment, which he suggests would be impossible under strict FFP rules. Kompany also points out the positive impacts City's owners have had on the community and economy of Manchester.

Bath Rugby has signed England Sevens international Jeff Williams, a 26-year-old with 36 tries on the World Series circuit, for the upcoming season. Previously playing for Hamiltons in Cape Town and France, Williams was an integral part of the England Sevens team that won the Tokyo Sevens tournament earlier this month. Bath head coach Mike Ford praised Williams for his dynamic play style, physicality, and suitability for the team's attacking ethos.

The article announces that Jared Leto has been cast as the Joker in the 2016 film "Suicide Squad," marking his first appearance as the character on the big screen since Heath Ledger. Notably, there is no Batman present in the film. Leto significantly transformed his appearance for the role, and "Suicide Squad" also features a prominent ensemble cast, including Will Smith, Margot Robbie, and various villains and anti-heroes. The film is set to be released in theaters on August 5, 2016.

Three Florida corrections officers and a former officer trainee have been charged with plotting to kill a former inmate upon his release from prison. The suspects were approached by an FBI informant who infiltrated the Traditional American Knights of the Ku Klux Klan, after they expressed a desire to eliminate the inmate due to a past altercation. The FBI staged a fake homicide scene to convince the suspects of the inmate's death, leading to their arrests. They now face up to 30 years in prison if convicted on one count of conspiracy to commit murder, with Florida's Attorney General vowing to address hate-based violence.

Manny Pacquiao's conference call discussing his upcoming fight with Floyd Mayweather was abruptly canceled due to technical difficulties, caused by a large number of boxing writers and broadcasters participating in the call. Pacquiao could only answer one question, and the rescheduled call will be held at a later time. American boxer Mayweather is scheduled to have his own media conference call on Wednesday.

The Miami Open celebrates notable milestones with grand cake presentations, with Serena Williams being the latest recipient for recording her 700th career victory. Andy Murray also received such a cake after winning his 500th match. Williams progressed to the semi-finals by beating Sabine Lisicki in a tight match, setting up a clash with Simona Halep, who defeated Sloane Stephens. Murray's elder sister Venus, despite reaching the semi-finals, was eliminated by Carla Suarez Navarro.

1. Beijing International Airport, also known as Daxing Airport, is set to launch the world's largest terminal, Terminal 1, in 2018, to accommodate rising numbers of Chinese tourists traveling the world. The terminal, designed by British-Iraqi architect Zaha Hadid, will encompass 700,000 square metres and manage 45 million passengers annually.

2. The design vision for Terminal 1 emphasizes open space and seamless passenger flow, featuring a six-tier structure with a pillar-free interior and a flowing roof. The terminal's central multi-layered courtyard will serve as a global meeting point for travelers.

3. Terminal 1's architecture is intended to represent a harmonious blend of Chinese landscape and culture, as part of showcasing China's rich heritage and future impact on the global tourism market. According to Bank of America Merrill Lynch's research, there were 109 million Chinese tourists in 2014, spending $164 billion, marking an increase from the 10 million outbound tourists in 2000.

Manchester United manager Louis van Gaal confirmed post-game that Wayne Rooney suffered a knee injury during their Premier League loss against Everton on Sunday. Rooney was replaced by Robin van Persie in the 88th minute and will be assessed to determine the severity of the injury. The defeat leaves United fourth in the race for automatic Champions League qualification and the injury may have given Liverpool an opportunity to close the gap.

1. Manchester City is reportedly interested in signing Arsenal midfielder Jack Wilshere, but he is recovering from ankle surgery and is yet to return to full fitness.
2. During his day off, Wilshere shared a photo on Instagram of his extensive shopping haul from Waitrose, which included food such as Seriously Fruity Mixed Berry Crisp, Special K, eggs, baked beans, and corn on the cob.
3. Wilshere humorously requested help from his Instagram followers to put away his shopping, expressing that the task was a Challenge after his "mad Monday aisle sweep."

A Venezuelan woman named Marleni Olivo threw a mango with her name, number, and a request for help written on it at President Nicolas Maduro to get his attention, and as a result, Maduro granted her a new apartment. This incident has become a viral topic in Venezuela, with some calling it a "manguicidio," a play on the words "mango" and "magnicidio," which means assassination of a powerful leader. However, Olivo denies any ill intent and states that her only aim was to own a home before she dies.

Argentine soccer star Carlos Tevez, who currently plays for Juventus in Serie A and previously played in the Premier League, believes it is harder to score goals in the Italian league compared to the Premier League. Tevez, who has scored 36 goals in Serie A since joining Juventus in 2013, criticized the midfields in the Premier League as non-existent and suggested that defending is better in Italy. After missing Juventus' match against Parma, Tevez stated that his task of scoring goals had become much more difficult. The former Manchester United and City striker also believes that his current Juventus team is more rounded than the one he played on when he won the Champions League with Manchester United in 2008, and believes they have the potential to match that achievement.

Yaya Toure, a Manchester City midfielder, was criticized by Jamie Carragher for not properly engaging in a defensive wall during a free-kick that resulted in Crystal Palace's winning goal at Selhurst Park. Toure was part of a five-man wall but was accused of ducking, while his teammates Fernandinho and Vincent Kompany appeared more attentive. The defeat further widened the gap between City and Chelsea in the Premier League, with the champions now nine points behind their rivals.

A 50-year-old Australian man died suddenly at the 101 Legian Hotel in Kuta, Bali, reportedly following a suspected heart attack. According to a restaurant employee, the man had earlier expressed feeling unwell before collapsing. Kuta, a popular tourist destination known for its long sandy beach, varied accommodation, and numerous restaurants and bars, attracts many Australian tourists. An autopsy is scheduled to determine the exact cause of death.

Richie Benaud, a former Australia cricket captain and commentator, passed away last week at the age of 84 due to skin cancer complications. A private funeral service was held in Sydney on Wednesday attended by close family and friends, including ex-players Shane Warne and Ian Chappell. The Australian Prime Minister Tony Abbott offered a state funeral, which Daphne Benaud declined, regarding it as a sign of respect for the impact Benaud had on millions nationally and internationally. Benaud's career marks include his Test debut in 1952, reaching 2,000 Test runs and 200 wickets, and spending 42 years commentating for the BBC. A memorial was held at the Australian Golf Club for his commentating colleagues, Channel Nine network executives, and past and present Test cricketers. He was revered by cricket fans worldwide for his unique commentary style.

A 16-year-old girl named Isobel Attwood has been missing for two days, and friends believe she is in Southampton with a man in his 20s. Isobel attempted to reassure her family through a Facebook post stating that she was safe but needed to get away. Police are concerned for her welfare and are asking for the public's help in finding her, as they believe she could still be in the Winchester or Southampton area.

Manchester City players face significant salary reductions of £500,000 per player if they fail to qualify for the Champions League this season. This is due to incentivized contracts that ensure financial fair play compliance. Their recent 169th Manchester derby loss to Manchester United leaves them in a precarious position, with Liverpool only four points behind. Manager Pellegrini admitted the team's performance, especially in the last three months, has been subpar, and they may miss out on signing top players like Paul Pogba due to this. In contrast, Manchester United's victory has boosted their confidence for the next transfer window.

Martin Skrtel, a defender for Liverpool, has denied rumors suggesting he would leave the Premier League club this summer, despite being linked to Wolfsburg and Napoli. Skrtel's agent has revealed that the only offer on the table is an extension of his contract with Liverpool, and there is little likelihood he will depart Anfield. Skrtel has made over 200 league appearances for Liverpool since joining in 2008.

A Texas-based CEO, Cheryl Rios, has faced criticism for stating on Facebook that a woman cannot be president due to her hormones and the potential to start a war. In her post, Rios pointed to biblical reasoning for her position but didn't reference any specific verse. Many on social media condemned Rios as a misogynist and a hypocrite, particularly given her leadership role. Rios stood by her comments, stating that she is entitled to her own opinions and that women can excel in various fields but not necessarily in the role of the president.

1. Atletico Madrid striker Mario Mandzukic, who was physically assaulted during the Champions League quarter-final first leg against Real Madrid, is expected to recover in time for the return leg at Bernabeu on Wednesday.
2. Mandzukic suffered injuries, including a cut to the nose from an elbow by Sergio Ramos and a punch to the stomach from Dani Carvajal, during the first leg that ended 0-0.
3. Despite the injuries, Atletico coach Diego Simeone expects Mandzukic to play alongside Antoine Griezmann in attack, with Griezmann in top form having scored both goals in the team's 2-1 La Liga victory over Deportivo La Coruna.

Jose Mourinho, despite preparing Chelsea players to counter Marouane Fellaini's threat, was informed by a hotel doorman that Fellaini was not playing due to him obtaining tickets from Eden Hazard. However, Mourinho discovered through Google that the doorman had mistakenly identified Fellaini's twin brother Mansour as Marouane. Ironically, Mansour Fellaini (not Marouane) played in the match at Stamford Bridge, which Chelsea won 1-0, moving them closer to the Premier League title. In the game, Kurt Zouma was given a specific task to contain Marouane Fellaini, but Mansour Fellaini was dealt with by Zouma in midfield.

Dawn Milosky, a 45-year-old resident of Beachwood, New Jersey, was rescued from an overturned and burning 2006 Toyota Solara convertible after being allegedly spotted driving erratically. Officers Mark Ehrenberg and Ricky Ferriola of the Kinnelon borough arrived at the scene, knocked the unresponsive Milosky free from her seat belt, and administered CPR. Shortly thereafter, the vehicle burst into flames. Milosky was charged with driving under the influence, having an open container of alcohol, reckless driving, and failure to stay in the right lane. She was subsequently airlifted to Morristown Medical Center, reportedly in stable condition.

A farmer in China is currently caring for a baby goat with six legs, which has been nicknamed the 'spider goat' and has gained national attention. The goat, which was born 20 days ago and weighs approximately 5kg, is reportedly healthy and playful, with an extraordinary appetite. Mr. Xiao, the goat's owner, considers the goat's unique condition a natural mutation and does not plan to take it to a vet to remove the extra legs.

West Ham United is eyeing a summer transfer of Javier Hernandez from Real Madrid, who recently scored a significant goal against Atletico Madrid. Hernandez, who has one year left on his contract with Manchester United, is not in their plans and may be available for around £7 million. West Ham has a list of younger transfer targets, including Sampdoria's Pedro Obiang, FC Sion's Moussa Konate, and Basle's Fabian Schar, ahead of their final season at Upton Park.

1. Stuart McCall, the interim manager of Scottish Championship club Rangers, has ruled out any discussions about his future before the end of the season, despite restoring a positive atmosphere and securing three straight wins.

2. McCall, who agreed to a deal until the end of the season with the aim of rekindling Rangers' promotion push, emphasized that his side has yet to achieve any tangible success.

3. The arrival of Shane Ferguson on loan from Newcastle is imminent, but McCall is cautious about Ferguson's immediate impact due to a long-term knee injury. The Northern Ireland international will likely need to build up his fitness with Under-20 games before featuring for Rangers.

Werder Bremen secured a 1-0 victory over Hamburg SV with a late Franco Di Santo penalty, keeping them in contention for a Europa League spot. The game saw Argentine Di Santo score his 13th goal of the season, while Hamburg's Valon Behrami was sent off. This victory moved Werder up to seventh place, while Hamburg remain in last place. Meanwhile, second-placed VfL Wolfsburg are set to try and reduce Bayern Munich's lead to 10 points, following Bayern's 2-0 victory, and Bayer Leverkusen sit in third place after their win over Hanover 96.

A two-year-old boy fell approximately 10 to 12 feet into a cheetah exhibit at the Cleveland Metroparks Zoo after being dangled over the edge by his mother. The toddler suffered minor bumps and bruises but was not attacked by the cheetahs. Witnesses claim the child was dangled over the railing, and the zoo plans to press child endangerment charges against the family on Monday. The exhibit was closed following the incident.

A Russian TV channel gave a mature rating to Hillary Clinton's first campaign video due to fears it might violate Russia's anti-gay propaganda law, which restricts discussions of gay rights around minors. The video, featuring a brief scene of two men holding hands, has sparked controversy since Russia's enactment of the law in 2013, which drew international criticism for its perceived discrimination against LGBTQ+ individuals. The law categorically banned "propaganda of non-traditional sexual relations" around minors.

Siem de Jong returned to action for Newcastle Under 21s after recovering from a collapsed lung, but was replaced at halftime during a 2-0 loss to Derby County. De Jong, who joined Newcastle last summer, has had a limited role in the first team. Meanwhile, Derby managed to secure a win with goals from Alefe Santos and Farrend Rawson, the latter returning after recovering from a torn thigh muscle and a collapsed lung surgery. De Jong, initially expected to miss the rest of the season, now has a slim chance of playing in the final six matches, but is unlikely to feature in the upcoming match against Tottenham.

Chef Ally Lees of Alfie Bird's restaurant in Birmingham has created a three-foot diameter omelette containing 12,000 calories and 945g of protein, which is 16 times the recommended daily intake for a man. The omelette, made with 150 eggs, is claimed to be the biggest ever cooked and is recommended for a group of no fewer than five to consume. The dish was prepared as a promotional offering for Easter.

Three Olympic gold medalists, Jessica Ennis-Hill, Mo Farah, and Greg Rutherford, will participate in the Sainsbury's Anniversary Games in London this summer, having won their golds during Super Saturday in 2012. This three-day event includes a two-day Diamond League meeting and the Sainsbury's IPC Athletics Grand Prix Final. Notably, Ennis-Hill is making her first appearance since giving birth to her son last year. Tickets for the public are now available for purchase on britishathletics.org.uk, with prices starting from £20 per adult and £12 for concessions for the July 24-25 dates, and £10 for the July 26 event.

In a Rio de Janeiro snack bar, customers were unknowingly consuming pastries filled with stray dog meat. police discovered numerous frozen dog carcasses at the establishment. The owner, Chinese Van Ruilonc, admitted to using the dogs for the fillings, claiming they were strays from the city. Additionally, officers found evidence of trafficked Chinese workers being forced to work in slave-like conditions within the establishment, and a cage where a worker was imprisoned. Further investigation revealed the presence of dog meat in the frozen 'pastels' fillings.

The article details the arrest of Ebony Dickens in Georgia, who posted a racially charged threat against white police officers on Facebook under the name Tiffany Milan. The threatening post, which was removed the day before her arrest, commented on Black-on-white killings and detailed plans to commit such acts. Police traced the post back to Dickens' identity, who was found, searched, and arrested at her residence, with a firearm and three computers confiscated. She was charged with disseminating information related to terrorist acts, placed under a $10,000 bond, and banned from social media.

PSV Eindhoven won the Dutch Eredivisie championship for the first time in seven years by beating Heerenveen 4-1, securing them 79 points and putting them beyond reach of second-placed Ajax Amsterdam. Striker Luuk de Jong scored two headed goals in the first half, with Memphis Depay adding a third with a stunning free-kick. Bottom side Dordrecht moved closer to relegation following a 3-0 loss at Vitesse Arnhem, while AZ Alkmaar sealed a place in the Europa League playoffs with a 3-1 home win over ADO Den Haag.

An 11-year-old boy named Shiva allegedly died from internal bleeding due to a brutal beating from his head teacher at Dwarika Prasad School in Railamau village, India. The teacher, Lalit Verma, admitted to slapping Shiva upon discovering stolen pencil and eraser. The incident is not the first instance of extreme corporal punishment resulting in the death of a student in India. For example, a 9-year-old in Burdwan, West Bengal was beaten with a stick by a private tutor and died shortly after, while a young boy in Bareilly, Uttar Pradesh was beaten and thrown out of a window onto a busy road after his parents failed to pay school fees on time.

A gastrointestinal illness has impacted around 100 passengers and five crew members on the Celebrity Infinity cruise ship, with symptoms including vomiting and diarrhea. The Centers for Disease Control (CDC) is investigating the cause, with CDC representatives scheduled to meet the ship in San Diego on Monday. Notably, this is the third reported outbreak of gastrointestinal illness on the Celebrity Infinity, which was built in 2001 and refurbished in 2011.

A Boston Terrier named Gizmo has gained internet fame by mastering a unique trick called paw-stand walking, where he walks on his hind legs while planting his front feet on the ground, developed while getting accustomed to new boots. Footage shows Gizmo taking a few steps forward and exhibiting graceful sidesteps before coming to a stop beside his owner. The video, which has been watched over 80,000 times, has brought smiles to viewers' faces.

New Orleans, a city known for its vibrant nightlife and festivals such as Mardi Gras and jazz fests, enacted a smoking ban in bars, casinos, and restaurants on October 1, 2021. The city's waitstaff and musicians will no longer have to work in smoky environments. The ban was passed unanimously by the New Orleans City Council in January, but some bar owners and customers have expressed concerns about potential revenue loss and the loss of smoking spots, respectively. A lawsuit has been filed against the ban, and a hearing is scheduled for next month.

Man Utd Under 21, captained by Adnan Januzaj, secured a hard-fought 3-1 victory against West Ham Under 21, moving four points clear at the top of the Under 21 Premier League. West Ham took an unexpected early lead through Reece Oxford's goal, their first away goal since September. However, Josh Harrop quickly equalized and moments later Joe Rothwell converted to put Man Utd ahead. Jordan Brown leveled the scores before half-time. Harrop capitalized on the West Ham goalkeeper's poor handling to score the winning goal for Man Utd, ensuring their continued dominance in the league.

1. Brisbane's Anglican Archbishop, Phillip Aspinall, has backed a local Catholic priest's appeal to abolish Queensland's 'gay panic' homicide defense, which allows murder charges to be reduced to manslaughter if the defendant claims their victim made a sexual advance.

2. In a statement after an Easter Sunday mass, Aspinall expressed that he finds this defense unreasonable and supports Father Paul Kelly's stance against it, emphasizing that violence is not a solution.

3. Beyond this issue, Aspinall also addressed instances of violence at anti-Islam rallies and church vandalism in Melbourne, urging everyone to resist reacting out of fear and to strive for a more peaceful and constructive response.

People magazine has named Sandra Bullock as the world's most beautiful woman of 2015 at the age of 50. In the accompanying interview, Bullock humorously dismissed the title, stating that real beauty lies in being a good person and making an effort to help others. The cover story focuses on her home life with her young son Louis and her continued efforts to stay healthy and fit beyond 40. The selection of Bullock, the oldest woman to receive the title, is seen as a reflection that beauty knows no age.

An improvised bomb explosion near Garowe, Somalia, killed six people, including four UNICEF aid workers, on Monday morning. The terrorist group Al-Shabaab claimed responsibility for the attack. In a separate incident on Sunday, three African Union troops were killed in an ambush in the Lower Shabelle region of Somalia. Both incidents were condemned by Somalia's President and UN officials, with the President denouncing the targeting of UNICEF workers as an attack on the future of Somalia.

A 45-year-old wildlife park owner, Gary Saurage, was called to remove a large, aggressive 400lb, 11ft-long alligator from a family's backyard pond in Beaumont, Texas. Saurage, seen in a photograph approaching the gator with his bare hands, managed to safely capture the creature. The incident was reported by Art Williams, who had initially spotted the gator over the Easter weekend. The alligator was later confirmed as a male, around 35 to 40 years old, and was taken to Saurage's wildlife park. Despite its size, this catch wasn't Saurage's largest; his largest alligator, nicknamed Kong, measures 12 feet and six inches.

On Saturday, five militants from the Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK) were killed and one was wounded in clashes with Turkish military forces in Agri, eastern Turkey. Four Turkish soldiers were also wounded. The fighting involved PKK militants attacking Turkish soldiers who were securing an area ahead of a spring festival. Turkish Prime Minister Ahmet Davutoglu and President Recep Tayyip Erdogan condemned the violence, with Davutoglu attributing it to the PKK's attempt to interrupt the peace process, and Erdogan calling it a terrorist attack. Last month, PKK leader Abdullah Ocalan urged his followers from prison to lay down their arms and join a peace congress. The decades-long conflict between the PKK and the Turkish state, which has resulted in an estimated 40,000 lives lost, is a dispute over Kurdish independence in Turkey, with some describing it as a battle for independence and others, a guerrilla war with terrorist acts.

Tragically, twin 18-month-old boys died after accidentally falling into a canal in Yuma, Arizona, on Friday morning. The incident is believed to be an accident and not foul play. Rescue efforts, involving the Yuma Fire Department, U.S. Border Patrol, and U.S. Marine Corps helicopters, lasted over an hour before the boys were pulled from the water and rushed to the hospital, where they were pronounced dead.

Orlando City, coached by Adrian Heath, has expressed interest in signing Manchester United's Javier Hernandez, a move that would likely be commercially beneficial due to Orlando's significant Latin-American fanbase. Hernandez, who has struggled at Real Madrid this season, is wanted by eight other European clubs, including Premier League teams like Southampton, Stoke, West Ham, and Everton, as well as Wolfsburg, AC Milan, Lazio, and Inter Milan. Meanwhile, Manchester United has made a revised contract offer to teenager Andreas Pereira, who has attracted interest from multiple European clubs, including Paris St Germain, Juventus, PSV Eindhoven, and Feyenoord.

Joel Burger, age 24, proposed to his long-time girlfriend Ashley King, and she accepted. Their shared last name, Burger-King, has fueled a year-long friendship that began in kindergarten. As a tribute to their playful nickname, and to add a unique twist to their wedding, they plan to serve drinks in personalized Burger King cups at their upcoming nuptials, if permitted by the global fast-food chain.

A previously unnamed hit band from the 1960s is linked to a notorious pedophile brothel in Battersea, South West London, as revealed in a 1964 police intelligence report. The band and Jimmy Savile, a well-known figure who frequently visited the brothel in the 1970s, may not have attended together. Det Supt David Grey, responsible for Operation Yewtree, began investigating the brothel in 2013, after it was mentioned in another report. Despite the link, Grey notes that it does not necessarily suggest a connection or warrant further investigation at the time.

A German Shepherd named Sadie has gained online attention for her unusual and entertaining piano performance at home in Alberta, Canada. She uses her paws to play a minimalist piece on the electric keyboard after turning it on with her nose. Her rendition, lasting approximately 20 seconds, displayed her musical inclinations, as seen in the video that has been viewed over 12,000 times. Sadie, who was previously rescued from a shelter and demonstrates a love for learning new tricks, is six years old and was recently taught to play the piano by her owner.

A shoplifting suspect, Ivan Balashov, was caught after taking a selfie while trying to steal a more desirable phone than the one he was initially browsing. When police were informed about the selfie, they identified and located Balashov, who was later found guilty and given a three-month suspended sentence.

The first official trailer for the documentary "Amy: The Girl Behind the Name" about the late British singer Amy Winehouse has been released. The documentary, set for a UK release on July 3, showcases early footage of Winehouse discussing her music career, her ambivalence towards fame, and her feelings about her music not representing her at the time she began writing. The film has been endorsed by Winehouse's family and features extensive unseen archive footage and previously unheard tracks. The film's producers were motivated to create a sensitive, honest, and non-sensational view of Winehouse's life, aiming to celebrate her musical legacy. A U.S. release date for the film has yet to be announced.

This week ("The Big Bang Theory" on Thursday 8 p.m. ET, CBS), two renowned actresses return to the show, potentially making it one of the best episodes this season. On Saturday May 2 at 11:30 p.m. on NBC, Scarlett Johansson hosts "Saturday Night Live" following the release of her new "Avengers" movie. In the Chuck Lorre dramedy "Mom" (Thursday 9:30 p.m., CBS), Allison Janney delivers another Emmy-worthy performance in the season finale. "Backstrom" (Thursday 9 p.m., Fox) wraps up its season, unsure if it will return for another season. "Blue Bloods" (Friday 10 p.m., CBS) finishes its two-part season finale, with questions lingering about its continuation. Lastly, "Younger" (Tuesday 10 p.m., TV Land) received a second season pick-up, and it's a great time to catch up with Sutton Foster and Hilary Duff while they navigate an unknown generational diversity issue.

The hit show "Downton Abbey" is concluding its run, but fans might take comfort in the possible return of the Dowager Countess as she appears in the new series "The Gilded Age," created by Julian Fellowes. Set in the late 1800s in New York, this US NBC show offers an opportunity to view the Countess in her youth. Potential returning characters include Robert, Earl of Grantham, Cora, and a young Violet. NBC seems enthusiastic about the show and it might debut as early as September this year. The sixth and final series of Downton Abbey airs later in the year on ITV, with American-born Cora also a potential candidate for a reappearance.

Steven Gerrard, who is set to depart Liverpool at the end of the season for LA Galaxy, is set to start in the FA Cup semi-final against Aston Villa at Wembley. This will mark his return to the side after serving a three-match ban. Gerrard, a key player for Liverpool with multiple trophies to his name, has been used sparingly by manager Brendan Rodgers this season but is described as a "special player" by Rodgers, and is considered ready for the semi-final.

A new, original Dr. Seuss book titled "What Pet Should I Get?" is set to debut on July 28, featuring the spirited brother and sister from "One Fish Two Fish Red Fish Blue Fish." The book's pre-orders have surpassed expectations, leading to an increased first printing of 1 million copies. The manuscript and illustrations for the new volume were found in the Geisel family's California home after Theodor Geisel's death in 1991 and have been set aside for publication since their rediscovery in 2013.

Jessica Carey, driving three hours to see her grandmother, surprised her with a tattoo of a childhood portrait of Patty Lawing on her forearm. Patty's emotional reaction was recorded on video, showing her overwhelmed and overcome with joy. The footage was captured in February but only recently emerged online. Jessica shared the video, highlighting the sentimental gesture to honor her favorite person in the world, her grandmother.

Annegret Raunigk, a 65-year-old mother-of-13 from Berlin, is set to make medical history by giving birth to quadruplets in the coming weeks, making her the oldest woman worldwide to have quadruplets. Having undergone fertility treatment for 18 months, Raunigk, a primary school teacher, expressed confidence in her ability to handle the impending birth, stating she "does not think she will have any problems." The identity of the babies' father remains unknown. Raunigk previously gained national attention in Germany after having her youngest daughter Leila at age 55, her 13 children being fathered by five different men.

Japan's space agency, JAXA, has announced plans to launch an unmanned rover aboard an Epsilon rocket to the moon by 2018, with an estimated cost of $83.4 million to $125 million. If approved, the mission aims to refine soft-landing technologies for potential manned expeditions to the moon or Mars. The rover will utilize face recognition software to identify lunar craters and optimize the landing spot, leveraging data from the SELENE craft, which orbited the moon in 2008. The initiative potentially positions Japan as a rising competitor in the lunar exploration field, mirroring recent achievements from Asian neighbors China and India.

1. The outbreak of dengue fever has impacted several top Brazilian football teams, with Corinthians striker Paolo Guerrero, Palmeiras reserve goalkeeper Aranha, and Santos striker Leo Cittadini being among the affected players.
2. Players have resorted to using insect repellent during practice sessions and clubs have sought assistance from health officials to inspect training centers for mosquito breeding sites.
3. The prevalence of dengue fever has significantly increased across Brazil in 2015, with more than 460,000 cases reported so far, accounting for almost 5,000 cases per day and resulting in over 130 fatalities according to the health ministry.

James Wilson, Manchester United striker, has expressed a desire to incorporate aspects of his teammates' styles into his own game. Specifically, he would like to replicate Wayne Rooney's free-kick ability, Robin van Persie's movement, and Radamel Falcao's instincts in the 18-yard box. Wilson has made 16 appearances for Manchester United this season, scoring once in the Premier League.

A triple tragedy occurred in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, where a 2-year-old was struck and killed by a van, the driver was later shot and died at the scene, and a 15-year-old was also shot and passed away. The shooting of the driver may have been in response to the child's death, though this is speculation, and authorities are still searching for the responsible party. The deceased driver was identified as Archie Brown Jr., a father of four who was a real estate entrepreneur and landlord.

The article presents a minor boy from Memphis, Tennessee, who has gained over 3,000 Twitter followers for posting pictures and videos depicting gang-related activities, including guns, drugs, and references to violence. His material has sparked criticism from the community and other Twitter users who view it as disturbing and damaging. The boy, in response, has defended his actions, stating that he has faced a challenging year and his critics are causing stress to his mother. Additionally, the article highlights the growing concern among authorities regarding the use of social media, such as Twitter, as a platform for perpetuating gang culture.

1. Former Redgum frontman John Schumann has expressed disappointment over the use of his song "I Was Only 19" at anti-Islam rallies organized by Reclaim Australia, as the song was written with themes of compassion, tolerance, and inclusiveness.

2. The song was allegedly played at one of the rallies, which aimed to oppose sharia law, halal tax, and Islamization, sparking a controversy that resulted in violence between protesters and anti-racism groups across Australia, with several arrests and minor injuries reported.

3. Notable figures such as Pauline Hanson and Federal Opposition Leader Bill Shorten have spoken out against the violence and discriminatory claims made during the rallies, emphasizing the importance of freedom of speech but condemning any use of violence and expressions of intolerance.

Emmanuel Adebayor, a forward for Tottenham, has stated his intent to continue at White Hart Lane, dismissing rumors of a move, and praised the Premier League. Despite a poor performance against Sheffield United earlier this season, he has only made 10 appearances and scored twice. Despite his reduced role due to the rise of Harry Kane, Adebayor remains determined to fulfill his contract with Spurs. His last Premier League goal for the team was versus Newcastle in October 2016.

Manchester City's manager, Manuel Pellegrini, is being urged to be given more time to revitalize the team's faltering performance, despite a bleak run that has put finishing in the top four in jeopardy. Notable pundit Stuart Pearce attributes City's troubles to a decline in form from key player Yaya Toure, with Sergio Aguero being the lone exception in an otherwise underperforming squad. Pearce remains optimistic about Pellegrini's future with City, recommending patience and a thorough squad overhaul for the summer.

Peter Moores, the current England coach under scrutiny following a poor World Cup campaign, expressed his willingness to work with Michael Vaughan if Vaughan becomes England's new director of cricket. Nottingham Forest is planning to make another attempt to sign Blackburn Rovers' striker Jordan Rhodes for £10 million this summer, following a previous loan deal rejection in March. A trio of dogs, including a Husky named Sky, two Springer Spaniels named Sadie and Marshall, performed a spontaneous musical ensemble in their owner's house in Bahama, North Carolina. The performance started with Sadie barking and was joined by Sky's clearer, more melodious howl. As the two dogs harmonized, the other Springer Spaniel wagged its tail excitedly. The dogs continued their performance, reaching a crescendo with all three pointing their noses to the sky and howling, before being called to stop by their owner. The video concludes with the dogs looking surprised at being interrupted.

The French free-climber Alain Robert, known as the 'French Spiderman,' ascended the Cayan Tower, the world's tallest twisted skyscraper, without a safety harness using just sticky tape and chalk. The 75-story tower has a twist of 90 degrees, and the climb took Robert an hour and a half. Spectators watched as he struggled to find footing on the narrow ledges, with the climb ending with Robert waving a flag in homage to the tower's developers. Notably, Robert has a history of illegal ascents and has faced arrests, imprisonment, and bans in various locations worldwide. Despite this, the Cayan Tower climb marks another daring feat in the climber's career.

An experimental cancer drug, AZDO5030, developed by Astra Zeneca and previously dropped due to poor cancer treatment results, may potentially reverse the effects of Alzheimer's. The drug restores synaptic connections and reduces inflammation in the brain, according to a study by scientists at Yale University. This development offers a new avenue for finding treatments for Alzheimer's, as the drug has already been proven to be safe for human use.

Harry Kane's attendance at the Under-21 European Championship is uncertain due to him being part of Tottenham's post-season friendly tour in Malaysia. The California Department of Public Health has declared an end to a measles outbreak that affected over 130 people since December. The outbreak started with visitors to two Disney theme parks in the state, and was controlled through prompt investigation, vaccination, and increased awareness among healthcare providers. Of the 81 patients for whom vaccination status was known, 70% were unvaccinated, highlighting the importance of immunization. Two additional measles cases were identified in April, but they had a different genotype from the outbreak strain.

A family-of-six in Argentina's San Miguel de Tucuman is being sought by police after they were seen riding on a single motorbike without helmets. The photograph shows a man holding the handlebars, three young children on the petrol tank, a girl and a woman seated behind him. Eyewitness Etel Ramirez Nazario considers their actions shocking and potentially dangerous. This incident follows a similar one in Junin, where a family of seven was spotted riding on the same motorbike, which has also been condemned online for its irresponsibility and danger. Andrea McVeigh, a 44-year-old social media manager, was left with severe facial injuries, including two three-inch gashes to her forehead, after being knocked down by a cyclist on a pavement in Bermondsey, south London. The cyclist fled the scene but was pursued by Andrea's husband. Met Police have issued CCTV footage of a cyclist they want to speak to in connection with the crash. Police are appealing for public assistance to identify the cyclist.

Hillary Clinton's father's headstone was found tipped over at the Washburn Street Cemetery in Scranton, Pennsylvania, a couple of days after Clinton announced her run for the White House. The headstone has been under the care of Paul McGloin since 1993. Police are investigating the incident, suspecting vandalism as the cause, although they are also exploring the possibility of it being weather-related. A California woman, Beatriz Paez, was terrified after a U.S. marshal grabbed her cell phone, smashed it, and kicked it away while she was recording police activity in South Gate, California. Paez has filed a complaint with local police but they have no authority over marshals. She is considering a lawsuit. The incident was captured on video by another woman. The U.S. Marshals Service is reviewing the incident and Janice Hahn, Paez's U.S. district representative, has written a letter to the outgoing U.S. Attorney General Eric Holder, requesting a federal investigation into the officer's actions.

Max, a one-of-a-kind husky-corgi cross, stands at 18.5 inches tall and is currently residing at the Dogs Trust in Basildon, Essex. Having been abandoned and with a low profile due to limited information about his past life, Max is described as gentle, intelligent, and big-hearted. The increased popularity of huskies is partly attributed to shows like Game of Thrones, but many owners are unaware of the specific care and commitment these breeds require, leading to abandonment.

In central London, Chilean pickpockets have emerged as the most effective thieves, with gangs targeting wealthy shoppers in the West End. According to undercover police, these individuals are often part of mixed teams that blend in with tourists or businessmen, making them difficult to trace. The Metropolitan Police, for instance, stopped two Chilean women wearing burkas after they were seen targeting rich Arab tourists in the Park Lane and Mayfair areas, finding €130,000 and £20,000 along with gold and diamond jewellery in their possession. London's busy shopping districts, such as Oxford Street, attract pickpockets from various countries, including Romania, Algeria, Bulgaria, and now Chile. Efforts are being made by plain-clothes police to combat pickpocket crimes in these areas, with many thieves arriving on a six-month visa before embarking on a "European tour."

A 20-year-old man miraculously survived a severe car crash in Southam, Warwickshire, despite sustaining head, chest injuries, and suspected leg fractures. His navy blue jeans were found under the overturned car after firefighters spent 25 minutes using cutting equipment to free him. The man was fully immobilized and airlifted to University Hospital Coventry and Warwickshire, with medics stating he was fortunate to be alive given the crash's severity. Firefighters assisted at the scene for roughly 45 minutes.

A 40-tonne pile of industrial waste, believed to be transported by three tractors and trailers, has been dumped by the side of the road in a Suffolk village, Walsham-le-Willows. This is deemed the worst case of fly-tipping in police officer PC Mark Bryant's 28-year career. Authorities are working together with the National Farmers' Union and the Country Land and Business Association to combat fly-tipping, and are currently working to clear the waste.

A man was Tasered at Toronto's Pearson International Airport after refusing to comply with security protocol and attempting to enter a restricted area. The incident happened while he was being denied boarding on a Turkish Airlines flight. In a video recorded by a bystander, the man appears disoriented and is visibly shocked after being Tasered. Authorities transferred him to a hospital under Canada's Mental Health Act, but it is unclear if they plan to pursue criminal charges against him.

The government jet carrying Serbia's president to Italy was forced to return to Belgrade after the co-pilot accidentally turned off the autopilot by wiping coffee off the instrument board during turbulence. This incident occurred due to the co-pilot, Bojan Zoric, inadvertently activating the emergency slat button, causing the plane to lose altitude. As a result, President Tomislav Nikolic's official visit to meet Pope Francis in the Vatican had to be cancelled. The pilot, Zoric, temporarily lost his license following the investigation into the incident.

In South Africa, more than 300 individuals have been arrested for deadly attacks on foreigners, resulting in thousands fleeing, with the incidents occurring mainly in Durban where mobs with machetes targeted immigrants. The government has strongly condemned the attacks and praised law enforcement for stopping further bloodshed. To help those affected, the Gift of the Givers charity is providing shelter in Johannesburg, where past anti-immigrant tensions have resulted in violent incidents. President Jacob Zuma has expressed support for the displaced foreign nationals.

In Revelstoke, Canada, skier Zach Birnie was filming the scenic mountain top with a helmet-mounted camera when he triggered a minor avalanche while making a controlled turn off-piste. The avalanche buried him in snow, and confusing, hazy footage shows him struggling to find the surface. After briefly disappearing beneath the snow, he eventually re-emerged, panting in shock but uninjured. Cornelia Accola from the WSL Institute for Snow and Avalanche Research SLF speculates that the avalanche may have been caused by the steep terrain and fresh snow. She advises that if someone finds themselves in a similar situation, they should aim to escape the avalanche area, let go of their ski poles, attempt to open their bindings, pull their knees toward their chest, and hold their arms in front of their face.

On the hottest day of the year, two men stripped off their tops before robbing an Esso petrol station in Town End, Caterham, Surrey, leaving with a staff member's mobile phone. Police have released CCTV images of the men, hoping for public identification. A third man, also in his 20s, has been arrested and released on police bail while the investigation continues. No one was injured during the incident that occurred around 7:45 pm.

The article discusses the Lada Niva 4x4, a rugged, affordable Russian vehicle that has gained popularity globally for its resilient nature and rough-and-tumble appearances. Despite its modest price of £13,395 (on the road), the Niva offers a functional, no-frills experience, featuring a plastic interior that is easy to clean after off-road adventures. Notably, the Niva is also available in a compact van format for £10,590. However, a potential downside is that Russian President Vladimir Putin, in a historic move in 2009, modified his Niva with a German engine, indicating a departure from the pure Russian legacy.

A lawsuit accuses the AIDS Healthcare Foundation, the nation's largest provider of HIV and AIDS medical care, of a $20 million dollar scam involving Medicare and Medicaid by offering employee and patient incentives for patient referrals. The alleged scheme was led by three former managers and is claimed to have started in 2010 at the company's California headquarters, spreading to programs in multiple states. The foundation, which operates in 36 countries, including a mass testing initiative, denies wrongdoing, with president Michael Weinstein stating the incentives are "mainstays of public health interventions." Three former managers, who were fired after raising concerns, have filed the whistleblower complaint.

A bearded dragon named Liz, owned by Shannen Hussein, appears to understand the question "Are you hungry?" and responds with a nod. Liz is rewarded with a superworm treat, one of her favorites. Shannen Hussein also cares for other pets, including a famous pet lamb named Winter, who is known for her antics on Vine videos, as well as multiple cats, birds, a snake, ducklings, turtles, a llama, and an emu, among others, on her hobby farm. After a meal, Liz is seen looking satisfied.

A 21-year-old aspiring country singer from West Virginia named Travis Hatfield has gained viral popularity after posting a video of him singing George Jones' hit to his uncle, Jamie Joe Cline, who has Down syndrome. Travis and Jamie often play music together, with the video showing them singing He Stopped Loving Her Today, and it has garnered over 410,000 views. Travis describes Jamie as a significant figure in his life and credits him for fostering his love for music. Travis aspires to become a country singer, and, encouraged by the viral video's success, he now receives interest from Nashville record labels.

High-wire artist Nik Wallenda plans to walk untethered on the moving Orlando Eye observation wheel on April 29, marking the latest daredevil stunt in his career, which includes walking across the Grand Canyon and Niagara Falls. The Orlando Eye, a new entertainment complex component, will open to the public on May 4 with panoramic views of central Florida from 30 air-conditioned glass capsules. This stunt differs from Wallenda's previous Ferris wheel walk due to the larger size of the wheel and his decision not to use a pole during the performance.

Bayern Munich's central defender Medhi Benatia is expected to miss between two and four weeks due to a muscle injury, potentially ruling him out for both legs of their Champions League quarter-final against Porto. Bayern Munich, led by Pep Guardiola, crushed Porto 6-1 in the Champions League quarter-finals, bringing their season goal tally to a stunning 115. These incidents have resulted in disruptions and delays for numerous passengers.

An off-duty Secret Service agent, Arthur Baldwin, was arrested early Friday morning in Washington D.C., charged with attempted burglary and destruction of property. Israel is developing a precision tunnel detection system, a first-of-its-kind equipment jointly developed by Elbit Systems and the Israeli Ministry of Defense. The new system has successfully passed initial tests and is expected to provide an additional layer of security. The exact timeline for the project's implementation has not been disclosed.

The primary school headteacher, Linda Shute, has implemented a rule prohibiting all drinks except water during school hours at Rowdown Primary School in New Addington, south London. This move has been met with opposition from some parents who claim their children dislike water and argue that they should have the right to choose what their child drinks. This water-only rule has previously caused an uproar at other schools, such as Valence Primary School in Dagenham, east London. The brawl led to the match being halted, and Torpedo ran out 3-1 winners after order was restored. Queens Park Rangers are planning to bring Dutch midfielder Leroy Fer back from a knee injury to bolster their efforts against relegation, despite his struggles with form and fitness since joining from Norwich in the summer. Fer, who was injured in mid-February, has returned to training and manager Chris Ramsey hints at his potential inclusion in the squad for the upcoming London derby against West Ham.
