He was taken to the hospital for x-rays, and his team reported he had pain in his arm and ribs. The remainder of Team Sky's riders were unharmed and are in good shape for the upcoming Paris-Roubaix race. Alexander Kristoff from the Katusha team took the win, as only 14 riders were able to contest the sprint finish following the crash.

Aston Villa players received messages of encouragement from fans, displaying them in their dressing room before the FA Cup semi-final against Liverpool. Jack Grealish, a 19-year-old player, appreciated the support on Twitter, and Brad Guzan also shared the contents of a message that instructed them to "fight like Lions." Grealish was included in the starting line-up due to impressive performances against Queens Park Rangers and Tottenham.

A 12-year-old boy in central China, known as Hanghang, was severely injured when his old phone exploded while he was using it as an alarm prior to school. The explosion exposed part of his jawbone and embedded fragments in his arms and legs. Doctors believe that the most common cause for the phone explosion was improper charging, leading to overheating and a sudden discharge of current. Hanghang is now receiving treatment in Ping Mei Group Hospital and is expected to require multiple surgeries for recovery.

Mike Rowe, the host of "Somebody's Gotta Do It," met Chad Pregracke, founder of Living Lands & Waters, a nonprofit dedicated to cleaning U.S. waterways. Pregracke, awarded CNN Hero of the Year in 2013, has led over 87,000 volunteers to collect 8.4 million pounds of trash since founding the organization in 1998 at age 23. Rowe toured Pregracke's 150-foot solar-powered living-working barge, made from a recycled strip club, and learned about Pregracke's 2015 mission to remove an additional 500,000 pounds of trash. Individuals who wish to contribute can visit LivingLandsAndWaters.org/Get-Involved/ for details.

The eerie, abandoned 11th-century town of Balestrino, located in Tuscany, Italy, was filmed using a drone. The video shows the town's picturesque landscape, including a castle on a hill and crumbling buildings. The town, which was once home to 800 inhabitants, was evacuated due to seismic instability, with a significant earthquake in 1887 causing severe damage. Today, it is known as one of Italy's most famous abandoned locations and is rumored to be haunted. The drone footage highlights the town's empty and haunting ambiance, with dark, empty windows contrasting the grandeur of the castle.

The article discusses the event in Anaheim, California, where J.J. Abrams and the cast of "Star Wars: Episode VII -- The Force Awakens" presented the film's trailer to an enthusiastic audience. Key takeaways include Han Solo and Chewbacca's return, a new planet characters visit called Jakku, hints of Luke and Leia's presence, less reliance on CGI compared to the prequels, and the use of practical sets. The new "Star Wars" film is set to release on December 18.

Former Toronto Mayor Rob Ford has announced that he will undergo an eight-to-ten-hour surgery to remove a cancerous tumor in his abdomen on May 11. The procedure comes after he completed five rounds of chemotherapy and nearly a month of radiation, which has shrunk the tumor significantly. Ford hopes to return to work as a city councilor in September and expressed gratitude to his medical staff, family, and the people of Toronto for their support.

A South African university, the University of Cape Town, has successfully removed a statue of the British colonialist Cecil Rhodes from its campus following weeks of protests led by students who view his legacy as racist. The students, led by the Student Representative Council, argue that Rhodes represents diversity, racism, and misogyny and should not be celebrated. However, some protesters in Pretoria argue this is an erasure of history and that more monuments should be erected rather than defiled ones. After the statue's removal, students marked the occasion with a celebratory march, with plans for further action in the future to make the university more Afrocentric.

Michael Phelps, the 18-time Olympic gold-medalist, made a winning return to competitive swimming in Arizona after a six-month suspension for a drink-driving conviction. He claimed victory in the 100 meters butterfly race at the Arena Pro Swim Series, finishing with a time of 52.38 seconds, outperforming Ryan Lochte. Despite missing this summer's World Championships, Phelps has expressed his intentions to compete in the 2016 Olympics in Rio de Janeiro.

A woman in Crown Heights, New York was found hanging from a fire escape outside her apartment building on Sunday morning and remained there for over an hour. Witnesses were traumatized and initially thought it was a prank. The woman is reported to have had mental health issues, and her identity is yet to be revealed. A neighbor described her as a social, kind individual. The incident has prompted calls to the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline for those in need of assistance.

1. In a Rhone Valley derby, Lyon and Saint-Etienne ended in a 2-2 draw with Clinton N'Jie, Romain Hamouma, and Christophe Jallet scoring for their respective teams.
2. Lille kept their pursuit of fourth place alive by beating Bordeaux 2-0 at home, with Nolan Roux and Adama Traore scoring the goals, while Montpellier secured a narrow 1-0 win over Caen, thanks to a header from Brazilian defender Hilton.
3. After the matches, Lyon are now tied for first place with Paris St Germain, while Saint-Etienne remain fifth. Lille are now just four points behind Bordeaux, and Montpellier have moved up to seventh.

1. Arsene Wenger was surprised by the significant contributions of Hector Bellerin and Francis Coquelin in Arsenal's late push for the Premier League title. He originally did not expect these players to play pivotal roles.

2. Bellerin, a 20-year-old Spanish full-back, scored a crucial goal against Liverpool and demonstrated impressive defensive skills against Raheem Sterling. Wenger commended Bellerin's maturity, particularly after he scored the opening goal in a key game against Liverpool.

3. Arsene Wenger initially wrote off Francis Coquelin, sending him on loan to Charlton before Christmas, but Coquelin has since proven to be a valuable asset to the team. Wenger acknowledged that Coquelin's role has been crucial in Arsenal's strong finish.

A two-hour remake of the cult classic film "The Rocky Horror Picture Show" is in development by Fox, with Kenneth Ortega serving as director, executive producer, and choreographer. This project, titled "The Rocky Horror Picture Show Event", is being produced by Fox 21 Television Studios and The Jackal Group, and it's intended to celebrate the 40th anniversary of the original film. The special is still casting-contingent, and it will be filmed in advance, but the air date is yet to be announced. This isn't the first attempt to adapt "The Rocky Horror Picture Show" for TV; a proposed 30th-anniversary adaptation in 2002 never materialized. This new adaptation comes after Fox's live musical production of "Grease" and NBC's planned live version of "The Wiz".

AS Roma has been ordered to partially close their stadium for their next home game due to offensive banners displayed during a recent match against Napoli. The banners, directed towards the mother of a Napoli fan who was killed in violent clashes last year, were deemed provocative and insulting. Roma won the match, but the club and their fans have faced punishment for the incident. The club's president has strongly condemned the actions and expressed sympathy towards the family of the deceased fan. The bereaved mother, Antonella Leardi, has called for an end to such incidents.

Ellen White, a Notts County player, experienced a significant career moment by scoring a stunning free kick against her former club Arsenal in the Women's Super League. The goal was a result of a unique setup at the training ground during a set-piece, but the buildup was marred by a moment of confusion involving Laura Bassett and Alex Greenwood. Despite her missed penalty that could have sealed a 2-0 advantage, White's goal and Arsenal's late equalizer by Chioma Ubogagu resulted in a 1-1 draw.

Arsene Wenger acknowledges discussions with Eden Hazard's agent in 2012, but opted against signing him as Arsenal couldn't match Chelsea's financial offer for the Lille star. Now in a standout season for Chelsea, Hazard is a top contender for the Player of the Year award. Wenger believes Alexis Sanchez, also a strong candidate, will challenge him for the title in the next season as well.

Stephen Akers-Belcher, the former Mayor of Hartlepool, was dismissed from his care manager role at Newcastle City Council due to gross misconduct. This was a result of him taking time off work to attend a funeral, but evidence showed he had attended an official function on HMS Warrior instead, which was 323 miles away. Akers-Belcher claims the dismissal was in response to whistleblowing allegations, but the council maintains the allegations were investigated and no further action was taken. Akers-Belcher has declined to comment on the visit to HMS Warrior and the Hartlepool meeting related to regeneration and tourism.

A senior doctor, Dr. John Parker, who had been working at an Australian-run Ebola treatment clinic in Sierra Leone, was taken to Westmead Hospital in Sydney after developing flu-like symptoms. Tests performed at the hospital have confirmed that he does not have Ebola, and no further testing is required. His employer, Aspen Medical, confirmed that he followed protocol by notifying authorities as a precaution. Over 10,000 deaths have been reported from the deadly Ebola virus in Guinea, Liberia, and Sierra Leone.

A nine-year-old boy, Frankie Franz, emulated Barcelona star Martin Montoya's impressive 27-yard, basketball-hoop goal by scoring it twice from his home garden. The duplication of the trick shot was inspired by a video of Montoya accomplishing the feat at Barcelona’s Ciutat Esportiva training ground. Frankie, who is a budding academy player with Dagenham and Redbridge Football Club, exhibited shock and disbelief following the successful attempt, with the ball bouncing off the backboard and going through the net below.

The Wisden–MCC Cricket Photograph of the Year 2014 features a diverse array of cricket images, showcasing the global popularity of the sport, from professional matches to amateurs playing on a Bangladesh rubbish tip. The winning image is by Matthew Lewis and it captures Dwayne Bravo's breathtaking full-length catch for the West Indies during the ICC World Twenty20 competition. Other notable entries include ordinary players from various countries, a high-altitude game on Mount Kilimanjaro, and everyday moments like afailed catch attempt in an English league game.

A New Jersey judge, Lawrence Jones, ruled in a custody case that a mother did not abuse her parental discretion by taking her 11-year-old daughter to a Pink concert in 2013, despite the father's objections. The judge noted that while Pink's performances may have some suggestive elements, they are not necessarily inappropriate for preteens. After considering the mother's reasoning for allowing her daughter to attend the concert and speaking privately with the girl, Jones found that the mother acted within the bounds of reasonable parental judgment, and the daughter's health, safety, and welfare were not compromised.

The article reports that an average property in Salcombe, Devon, now costs more than that in London, making Salcombe the most expensive place in the UK to buy property. This above-average cost is even more for properties with water views, where the average value exceeds £2 million. Salcombe, nicknamed 'Chelsea-on-Sea', is popular for its yachting and sailing activities, fresh seafood, and stunning beaches. To experience Salcombe without high costs, hotel accommodations can be found from £425 per night.

Celtic have expressed dissatisfaction with the SFA over ticket prices for their Scottish Cup semi-final against Inverness Caledonian Thistle, particularly for the North Stand which is priced at £23 compared to other parts of the stadium. In a statement, Celtic argued that the pricing should be reviewed and lowered. The SFA has responded that the pricing has remained unchanged for the past four years and all four participating clubs were consulted on ticket pricing. Celtic manager Ronny Deila focuses on preparing his team for their SPL clash with St Mirren on Friday.

A student named Rebecca Rice, who experiences severe anxiety during exams, was permitted to bring her 11-year-old Labrador, Holly, into her GCSE French oral test at Bodmin College in Cornwall. Holly's presence helped Rebecca manage her nerves, and this strategy was one of several methods used by the school to reduce exam-related stress.

Anders Lindegaard, the Manchester United goalkeeper, enjoyed a day off with his wife Misse Beqiri, a Swedish model, whom he married last year in Mauritius. Despite struggling for playing time at United, Lindegaard frequently shares photos of his family on Instagram. Misse Beqiri, who has a large Instagram following, is a well-known model with Albanian roots. Despite limited minutes at Old Trafford, Lindegaard has been linked with a move away, but has yet to leave the club.

Manchester United goalkeepers David de Gea and Victor Valdes, following a recent impressive win against Manchester City, took a break from training to visit a theme park, basking in the English sun. The Red Devils have experienced a rollercoaster season, initially struggling to make the top-four but emerging as potential second place contenders in the Premier League. However, the future of both goalkeepers remains uncertain.

A 75-year-old piano teacher, John Goodwin, shot himself outside the Rockingham County Superior Courthouse in New Hampshire while awaiting a jury's verdict on charges of sexually assaulting an underage student. Goodwin, who pleaded not guilty, allegedly repeatedly assaulted the student, who is now 24, and the trial began this week. His condition following the self-inflicted gunshot wound is currently unknown. The jury was still deliberating at the time of the incident, and it's unclear if they were aware of Goodwin's actions. Further information regarding the incident is expected to be released by the New Hampshire Attorney General's Office later in the evening.

Amazon has removed a game called "Rescue the Anorexia Girl" from its platform after it received widespread criticism. The game, which was marketed by SmartTouch Media, invited players to throw food at a cartoon character with anorexia. Social media users and advocates for eating disorder awareness were outraged, noting that the game trivialized a serious mental illness and could potentially discourage individuals from seeking help.

Researchers are working to replicate the cognitive abilities of honeybees to power drones, with the aim of creating a robot that thinks, senses, and acts like them. The Green Brain Project, a collaboration between the Universities of Sheffield and Sussex, is leading this endeavor, and they have so far managed to clone the part of the honeybee's brain responsible for sight. They have built and tested three quadcopters and one ground robot, and their current projects include navigation tests and development of a Ground Control Station. The ultimate goal is to use these drones for tasks such as crop pollination and search and rescue missions.

A newly-wed Air Malta crew, a pilot and a cabin crew member, took their guests on a romantic fly-over of the Mediterranean, with the plane forming the shape of two giant hearts and covering Malta and the Italian coast. The unique flight path was reportedly to celebrate their marriage, as indicated by the 'Just Married' status on the airport's arrivals board. Some aviation enthusiasts speculated that the flight was a training exercise, while others praised the event as a creative PR stunt or a romantic gesture.

In Kristiansand Zoo, Norway, a five-year-old giraffe named Melvin was fatally gored by an eland antelope after getting its head stuck in a fence. The incident occurred on Easter Monday, and around 30 witnesses, including children, saw the unprovoked attack. Melvin was a beloved zoo resident, having been named in a national newspaper contest at the time of his birth in 2010. Zoo officials expressed sadness for the loss and veterinarians attempted to save Melvin, but he died at the scene. The reason for the attack remains unclear.

A restaurant in Leuven, Belgium, charged a mother 36p for heating up her baby's feeding bottle, sparking outrage on Twitter and earning the restaurant manager the title of 'stingiest boss in Europe.' The mother had gone to the Rubens eatery with her family and was shocked to find a charge for the bottle-warming service on her bill, which totaled around £20. The restaurant chain later explained that such a charge would only occur if customers are explicitly informed that the service is paid.

North Korea's cargo ship, the Mu Du Bong, was detained by Mexico due to its ownership company, North Korea's Ocean Maritime Management, allegedly evading United Nations sanctions. Mexico defended the decision, stating it adhered to international obligations as a responsible UN member state. The 33 North Korean crew members are currently staying at a hotel in Tuxpan, Mexico, and are scheduled to return to North Korea with assistance from their embassy. This situation contrasts with a previous incident involving the Chong Chon Gang ship in 2013, where Panama found undeclared weaponry from Cuba buried in bags of sugar, which led to the ship's seizure and the crew's detainment for months.

Prime Minister David Cameron will announce an additional 600,000 childcare spaces at a cost of £350 million to help offset increasing childcare expenses. His speech emphasizes that high childcare costs have hampered employment opportunities, particularly for second earners. To fund the extra childcare places, the Conservatives plan to reduce tax relief on pension contributions for individuals earning above £150,000. The new initiative will offer 30 hours of free childcare per week for three- and four-year-olds, reducing costs for working families by £5,000 annually and allowing them to work an extra 78 days annually without incurring childcare expenses. The measures are part of the Conservative Party's larger goal of promoting work as a means to combat poverty.

Manchester City's young squad reinforced their 3-0 first-leg lead against Leicester City with two late goals from Isaac Buckley and Brandon Barker, securing a Youth Cup final spot. Layton Ndukwu's penalty for Leicester momentarily reduced the deficit, but City's responses through Buckley and Barker cemented their 5-1 aggregate victory. The final against Chelsea, a repeat of their last Youth Cup final 7 years ago, is scheduled for later this month, with the first leg at the City Football Academy Stadium on April 20.

Russian President Vladimir Putin, during his annual Q&A session, dismissed Western sanctions as an attempt to limit Russia's development, not just relating to Ukraine and Crimea. He defended the sale of a sophisticated air defense system to Iran, stating it would not pose a threat to Israel, but rather be a defense weapon. The event, criticized as a staged imitation of democracy, is a platform for Putin to address the public and the world, with 2.4 million questions submitted this year. Notably, last year, Edward Snowden appeared by video link, addressing Putin on Russia's surveillance practices.

Aston Villa manager Tim Sherwood will evaluate Gary Gardner's ability during pre-season after a successful loan spell at Nottingham Forest. Gardner, who is eager to impress, scored a noteworthy free-kick in front of Sherwood during a game against Watford. Originally a part of Villa's academy, Gardner hopes to make an impact at the club following a contract extension despite previous serious knee injuries.

A stampede occurred at a nightclub in Santiago, Chile, during a British punk band Doom's performance, leading to the death of three individuals and injuries of a dozen more. The crowded entrance caused a structure inside the building to collapse, according to Police General Hugo Insulza. Seven people were critically injured, and several individuals have been arrested in connection with the tragedy. Doom, a Crust Punk band, is known for songs like "Anti-Social" and "Raining Napalm."

Bayern Munich advanced to the semi-finals of the German Cup after a 5-3 penalty shoot-out victory over Bayer Leverkusen, but manager Pep Guardiola expressed concern about their lack of scoring touch in recent games, attributing it to the absence of Franck Ribery and Arjen Robben. Robben is out until May due to a stomach muscle tear, while Ribery is recovering from an ankle injury and his return date is uncertain. Guardiola believes the team lacks players suitable for one-on-one situations with Ribery and Robben missing. The team will face Eintracht Frankfurt in the Bundesliga this Saturday, and Guardiola will be hoping to address the scoring issue. The team's only goal over their last three matches came from Robert Lewandowski in a 1-0 win against his former club Borussia Dortmund, and they will meet again in the semi-final.

Derry Mathews' world title challenge is in doubt due to Richar Abril's withdrawal for the second time, potentially jeopardizing Abril's WBA lightweight belt. Mathews, who recently secured a fifth-round knockout against Gyorgy Mezei Jnr in Liverpool, might still fight for a version of the title on April 18 in his hometown. Discussions are underway between Mathews' promoter, the WBA, and Abril's representatives regarding the title's current status, with Mathews expressing disappointment over Abril's inability to commit to the fight.

The article discusses a YouTube and Instagram video featuring an English Bulldog named Hazel. In the video, Hazel jumps onto a washing basket, causing it to topple over and sending her and some clothes onto the floor. Despite the mishap, Hazel continues exploring the basket and chewing its edges, ending the video staring innocently at the camera like butter wouldn't melt. The authors note that Hazel is often seen in other videos on Hazel's owner's social media accounts, where she is documented while discovering new things, such as looking at her reflection for the first time, playing on a skateboard, or trying on a collar.

The six-part BBC drama Wolf Hall, airing in the U.S. for the first time, has been criticized by American Catholic bishops for its 'prejudice-laden presentation of the past,' particularly its portrayal of historical figures like Thomas Cromwell and Thomas More. The bishops accuse the series of adopting an anti-Catholic perspective, and view the character depictions as distorted and unrepresentative. Some U.S. media, on the other hand, have looked forward to the drama, especially the performance of Damian Lewis as King Henry VIII. However, a critical review in The Washington Post warns of a potential ideological bias in the adaptation of Hilary Mantel's novel, which could compromise the historical accuracy and the valuable lessons from that era.

Today, Fort Hood victims, including Staff Sergeant Shawn Manning, are to receive Purple Heart medals, yet there are claims they are being denied crucial financial support. Manning, who was shot six times during the 2009 attack, alleges he has been denied benefits due to the Army rejecting his claims that his injuries were sustained in the line of duty. The Army rejects his injuries as combat-related since the 2015 National Defense Authorization Act does not offer combat benefits for those permanently disabled in attacks inspired or motivated by foreign terrorist organizations. Manning fears other survivors of the shooting rampage will be in a similar position and may miss out on $800 a month in benefits. The Army stated that Purple Heart Medal recipients would receive benefits to which they are legally entitled, and no final decision has been rendered in Manning's case. It is known that Army psychiatrist Major Nidal Hasan, the perpetrator of the attack, had exchanged emails with Anwar al-Awlaki, an al-Qaeda spokesman, and his actions were praised by al-Awlaki as a heroic act against the U.S. fighting against Islam.

1. Newcastle United head coach John Carver is facing intense criticism from supporters due to the club's poor performance and perceived lack of initiative from owner Mike Ashley.
2. Carver, having taken over a depleted and disinterested squad, believes his job is the hardest in football, despite reported plans for Derby County's Steve McClaren to take over in the summer.
3. Fans are planning to boycott the home match against Spurs as a protest against Ashley's management, but Carver has urged them to support the team instead. Fans organizing the boycott plan to gather outside the Gallowgate End before and after the game, and in Leazes Park during the match.

Jordan Spieth, a 21-year-old American golfer, has won the 2015 Masters tournament at Augusta, breaking several records including becoming the first to reach 19 under par. He had maintained a four-shot lead on the final day and held on to claim the title. As a junior player, Spieth was the only American besides Tiger Woods to win two US Junior Amateur titles and gained entry into a PGA event at just 17. After turning professional, he won the PGA Tour Rookie of the Year award and has continued to rise in the ranks, finishing as a low amateur in the 2012 US Open and tying for 10th on the PGA Tour money list by the end of the 2013 season. Off the course, Spieth is in a committed relationship with his high school sweetheart Annie Verret and recently purchased a $2.3 million mansion in his hometown.

Beatrice Tollman, the founder of a luxury hotel chain, donated £20,000 to the Conservative party in the UK, but her past involvement in tax evasion charges has come to light, which may cause embarrassment for Prime Minister David Cameron. Her husband, Stanley Tollman, had previously pleaded guilty to tax evasion and spent five years fighting extradition. The Conservative party has announced they will return donations from the Tollmans following these revelations.

A marketing coordinator named Poppy Smart reported sexual harassment to police after enduring daily wolf-whistling and sexist comments from builders during her commute in Worcester city center. She felt the wolf-whistling was intimidating and compared it to racial discrimination. The police had followed up Miss Smart's complaint as a possible incident of anti-social behavior, but no further action was taken. Wolf-whistling, although not a specific offense, can potentially be convicted as a breach of the peace. Despite some companies banning wolf-whistling, it persists as a form of everyday sexism, according to activists.

A UK teenager named Lily Sharp pranked her own mother by pretending to have been kidnapped, referencing the Liam Neeson film Taken. She convincingly created a narrative where a stranger entered their home, took her phone, and demanded a ransom. Her mother was completely fooled and called the police, but Lily eventually revealed the prank to her mother, who was not amused. Despite not receiving praise from her mother, Lily's prank gained widespread attention on social media.

In the first ODI of a series between Bangladesh and Pakistan in Dhaka, Bangladesh won by 79 runs. Tamim Iqbal and Mushfiqur Rahim scored centuries for Bangladesh, setting Pakistan a target of 330 for victory. In response, Pakistan struggled to reach this total, losing six wickets for 250 runs, with Arafat Sunny and Taskin Ahmed taking three wickets each for Bangladesh. The second ODI will take place on Sunday in Mirpur.

Todd Kincannon, a 33-year-old attorney and former South Carolina Republican Party executive director, has been arrested and charged with criminal domestic violence. The arrest warrant alleges that Kincannon grabbed his wife's arm and threatened to kill her, himself, and her family during an incident in March. A bond hearing is scheduled for the following day. Additionally, it was reported that his wife has evidence of verbal abuse and possible domestic abuse from Kincannon, including over forty-eight hours of audio recordings and photographic evidence. Kincannon has gained a reputation on Twitter for sending inflammatory tweets that have been criticized for their racist and sexist content, including a tweet last September that supported physical violence against a woman involved in an NFL scandal. Kincannon appears to have deleted his Twitter account following his recent arrest.

Jordan Spieth, fresh from winning the Masters and breaking Tiger Woods' record, is competing at the RBC Heritage Classic this week. Spieth, 21, dealt with a media frenzy following his victory and had a busy schedule of 26 appearances and interviews in 25 hours. Despite the excitement, Spieth maintains his focus on climbing the world rankings, particularly catching up to Rory McIlroy for the No. 1 spot. Spieth has had previous success at the RBC Heritage, finishing ninth in 2013 and 12th last year. He is playing without having had any practice on the course due to his busy schedule post-Masters win.

Samantha Cameron, wife of former British Prime Minister David Cameron, has demonstrated her affinity for the American psychedelic rock band Poliça, despite their music's often violent and unconventional themes, which contrast sharply with her aristocratic background and conventional life in Downing Street and the Cotswolds. The group's inspirations include Shulamith Firestone, a radical feminist known for her theories rejecting traditional gender roles, pregnancy, and childbirth. Poliça's recent album, Shulamith, pays tribute to Firestone, whose image appears bloodied on the album cover.

1. The Australian government plans to impose a 10% goods and services tax (GST) on movie and music downloads from streaming services like Netflix and Apple, potentially generating billions of extra dollars in revenue.

2. This new tax may also apply to online purchases under $1,000 from overseas, affecting companies such as Google, Microsoft, Amazon, and eBay.

3. Consumer advocacy group Choice suggests that the government should address the high domestic costs of TV shows, music, and movies, and make it easier to access them, rather than imposing the GST on digital goods. Netflix has indicated it will increase its service fee in response to any new laws or regulations.

Stephen A. Smith, an ESPN First Take anchor, has faced criticism for defending boxer Floyd Mayweather Jr., who has a history of domestic violence. In a discussion about Mayweather's upcoming fight, Smith argued that Mayweather's boxing career should be viewed independently from his domestic violence history. He suggested that fellow anchor Cari Champion's disagreement with this stance was due to her being a woman, sparking backlash. This is not the first time Smith has been controversial on this topic; in a previous episode, he allegedly victim-blamed in the Ray Rice scandal discussion.

A 12-year-old boy named Mahendra Ahirwar from India has a rare condition that causes his head to hang perpetually at a 180-degree angle due to a weak backbone, which makes him unable to stand or walk. His parents, who work as laborers, have consulted over 50 doctors across India but have yet to find a diagnosis or treatment, leaving them despairing and wishing for their son's death as an alternative to his suffering. Community members have blamed Mahendra's condition on his father's past sins, which adds to the family's hardship. Despite this, the father remains hopeful for medical intervention to improve his son's life. A consultant, Dr. Shashidhar Tatavarthy, has suggested that Mahendra may have a muscular disorder but a conclusive diagnosis can only be made following a comprehensive investigation.

1. Switzerland ranks as the world's happiest nation, according to a new study on global wellbeing, due to its healthy GDP figures, strong social bonds, and increasing life expectancy.

2. Iceland has improved its ranking significantly, moving from ninth in 2013 to second this year, thanks to factors like beautiful scenery, cultural history, and perceived generosity.

3. The World Happiness Report, which considers factors beyond wealth, found that countries at the bottom of the list are primarily those experiencing war, civil conflict, or extreme poverty. The least happy countries include Syria, Burundi, and Togo.

The article previews the upcoming Premier League match between Burnley and Arsenal at Turf Moor. Burnley's midfielder Matt Taylor could potentially make his return from a long-term achilles injury, while Ross Wallace and Steven Reid might also be available. However, Dean Marney and Kevin Long remain ruled out. Arsenal's Laurent Koscielny and Wojciech Szczesny face fitness tests ahead of the match. If Koscielny passes, he will play for the Gunners. Jack Wilshere, Mikel Arteta, Abou Diaby, and Mathieu Debuchy are also back in contention for the match. Key statistics include Arsenal's seven-game unbeaten streak in the Premier League, Burnley's propensity for fewer goals in the final 15 minutes at Turf Moor, and Olivier Giroud's impressive performance with 10 goals in his last 10 matches for Arsenal. The match kicks off on Saturday at 5:30 PM and will be broadcast on Sky Sports 1.

The article previews the upcoming Premier League match between Tottenham Hotspur and Aston Villa at White Hart Lane, providing information on team news, provisional squads, betting odds, and Opta stats. Tottenham will be without Kyle Walker and Hugo Lloris due to injuries, while Jan Vertonghen is a doubt for the match. Aston Villa will be missing Alan Hutton, Ashley Westwood, Scott Sinclair, and Carles Gil, but Aly Cissokho could return. Christian Benteke has been in form for Aston Villa, scoring seven goals in his last five Premier League appearances. Structurally, there is a focus on the team news for both sides, the possible return of key players, and individual key players' statistics.

The article previews the upcoming Premier League fixture between Liverpool and Newcastle United at Anfield, providing team news, squad lists, betting odds, and Opta stats. Liverpool will be without Mamadou Sakho due to a hamstring injury, but Emre Can returns from suspension. Sturridge and Balotelli are expected to be available. Newcastle's Daryl Janmaat should play despite an injury scare. Rolando Aarons and Siem de Jong are unavailable. The match kicks off on Sky Sports 1 on Monday at 8pm. Odds favor Liverpool, and key stats indicate Liverpool has not let Newcastle win a league double since 1993-94, and Newcastle has conceded at least one goal in their last 19 Premier League games at Anfield. Jordan Henderson has scored in four of his last five Premier League appearances for Liverpool. Newcastle's Vurnon Anita has been substituted at half-time three times this season. Raheem Sterling has already made four more starts for Liverpool this season than in the whole of 2013-14.

1. Nick Clegg, the leader of the Lib Dems, has attributed the party's dwindling poll ratings to a range of factors such as protest voters, coalition with the Tories, and public sector workers dissatisfied with pension changes and job cuts, while minimizing the impact of policy decisions like tuition fees.

2. In the interview with The Economist, Clegg admitted that areas where the Lib Dems had strong support in 2010, particularly 'virulently anti-Conservative' ones, have become 'Lib Dem deserts,' and the party is currently focusing its campaign on regions where it still has some support.

3. The Tories have criticized Clegg for blaming everyone but himself for the Lib Dems' downfall, labeling his comments as an example of him being 'like a petulant child.' Despite this, Clegg continues to assert the Lib Dems' desire to manage education if they form part of a coalition government post-May 7.

The divorce of chef Bobby Flay and actress Stephanie March has allegedly grown more complex, with claims that Flay had a three-year affair with his assistant, Elyse Tirrel. However, Flay's business partner, Laurence Kretchmer, has dismissed these allegations, stating that if such an affair were ongoing, he would be aware. The story, allegedly originating from a leaked letter, is part of a larger disagreement over a prenuptial agreement. Camellias are versatile, evergreen shrubs known for their contrasting foliage and bright flowers. They are easy to grow in acidic, free-draining soil, but mope in alkaline or neutral ground, in which case they should be grown in containers with ericaceous compost. Camellias flower over a long period and can be pruned or trained in various ways such as on walls or as hedging. Potted camellias may lose their charm after five to six years, but can be easily propagated through root cuttings. Some popular camellia varieties include Adolphe Audusson, Alba Simplex, St Ewe, Donation, and Williamsii hybrids like St Ewe. Camellias require moderate watering, magnesium supplements, and protection from frost. They are particularly beautiful and hardy in cooler climates such as Lincolnshire.

The article discusses the majestic greater adjutant stork that resides over the Boragaon landfill, one of the largest dumping grounds in India, located in Guwahati. Approximately 100 families live in this 94-acre landfill, searching daily for treasures such as plastic, metal, and bones, using hooks to sort through the garbage, which can reach two or three stories high. Despite challenging living conditions with no electricity, no running water, and an overabundance of trash, the residents of Boragaon are described as content, loving, hopeful, and spiritual, with some children attending school on scholarship. Photographer Timothy Bouldry, based in New Hampshire, has found his work photographing and teaching in landfills, such as Boragaon and La Chureca in Nicaragua, to be the most fulfilling, seeing it as a form of gratitude to the informal recyclers around the world.

The article discusses a recent study conducted at the University of Reading, which found that chewing gum can help reduce the likelihood and intensity of an earworm, or catchy song that refuses to leave one's mind, and may extend to other unwanted thoughts. In the study, 98 volunteers were played catchy tunes such as Play Hard by David Guetta and Payphone by Maroon 5. Participants who chewed gum while being asked to think of the songs reported thinking about them less frequently and less intensely than those who did not chew gum. The researchers suggest that this effect might be due to interfering with one's inner speech, potentially providing a strategy for managing symptoms of obsessive-compulsive and similar disorders. However, further research is needed to confirm these findings.

The study conducted by Swedish and British researchers suggests that consuming two cups of coffee daily could reduce by half the risk of breast cancer reoccurrence in women recovering from the disease, particularly for those on hormonal therapy drug tamoxifen. However, the researchers emphasize the importance of taking prescribed medication and drinking coffee in moderation.

Authorities in greater Sydney are planning to control a large population of feral rabbits, considered a pest, by using carrots laced with a deadly virus known as Calicivirus or Rabbit haemorrhagic disease (RHD). The rabbits cause significant damage to agriculture and the environment. The strategy has been implemented annually for the past nine years to manage the population. Rabbits under one year old have a higher chance of surviving, but about 70-100 percent of rabbits die once infected with the calicivirus. The program aims to reduce rabbit numbers before damage becomes too severe. Pet owners are encouraged to vaccinate their domestic rabbits to protect them from the virus, which does not harm cats, dogs, or humans. Rabbits, introduced to Australia by British settlers, breed quickly and can be found in various habitats across the country.

Ocean photographer Lloyd Meudell specializes in capturing the surreal, dream-like explosion of ocean foam on Kiama beach and surrounding areas on the south coast of NSW. He starts his day during the beautiful morning or evening hours, drawing inspiration from artists like Salvador Dali. Despite numerous requests, he does not reveal his camera settings, preferring to keep it a secret while encouraging future photographers to learn about the ocean and surfing before taking up this type of photography.

Bayern Munich suffered a 3-1 defeat in the first leg of their Champions League quarter-final against Porto, with goals from Ricardo Quaresma (penalty) and Jackson Martinez (2). Bayern manager Pep Guardiola attributed the loss to injuries in his squad, while Porto manager Julen Lopetegui expressed optimism about reaching the semi-finals. Martinez, who returned from injury for the game, was a constant nuisance for Bayern's defense and scored Porto's third goal. Quaresma also praised Porto's teamwork and effort. The return leg will be played next Tuesday in Munich.

The Curiosity Rover has discovered multi-colored veins on Mars, specifically at a site called 'Garden City' on Mount Sharp. These veins, which range up to 6cm in height, are believed to be remnants of Mars' watery past. Scientists recognize that both bright and dark minerals found in these veins provide insights into secondary fluids that moved through the region post-rock formation. The darker veins, in particular, have puzzled researchers. This study suggests that Mars once contained more water than the Arctic Ocean, with the red planet maintaining its water for over 1.5 billion years. However, over time, Mars has lost 87% of its water, leaving it dry and barren today. The findings imply that Mars had ample water and time for life to thrive but eventually dried out.

A 25-year-old man, Carl Bradey, is being hailed as a hero after rescuing a three-year-old girl from a house fire that damaged his body extensively. The fire, initially sparked by a candle, destroyed Bradey's rental property in Palmerston North last month. He suffered nerve damage in his right arm and severe burns across his entire body. Bradey, who is currently staying with his mother, has undergone multiple skin grafts and surgeries and his family has set up a crowdfunding page to aid him in his recovery. Fire experts advise using candles in solid holders and away from inflammable materials.

1. Thousands of olive trees in Italy's Puglia region are being cut down due to an outbreak of the xylella fastidiosa bacteria, which has led to a 35% drop in olive oil production and is expected to cause global shortages and price increases.

2. The government's plan to destroy infected olive trees has been met with opposition from Puglian growers, who argue that it won't halt the spread of the bacteria.

3. The bacterium, which originated in the Americas, has infected over 800,000 trees in the Salento region of Puglia and is feared to spread to other Italian and Mediterranean olive-producing areas if drastic action isn't taken. The bacterium makes plants shrivel and incapable of bearing fruit. Exports of Italian olive oil are significant in many countries worldwide, with Italy holding a 51% share in the USA market among others.

A border guard was killed in a gunfight with militants at the Saudi Arabia-Yemen border, marking the first reported military death for Saudi Arabia since launching airstrikes against Yemeni rebels. Meanwhile, Houthi rebels seized the presidential palace in the Yemeni port city of Aden, with Yemeni special forces loyal to former President Ali Abdullah Saleh attempting to secure the city. Additionally, U.S. Navy warships are patrolling off Yemen to monitor suspicious shipping, particularly potential weapons shipments from Iran to Houthi rebels.

A 53-year-old man, Muhammed Tahir, was convicted of sexual assault on a young woman on the London Underground. He was caught rubbing his crotch and pot belly against the victim during rush hour. Despite the grave nature of the crime, the judge decided not to imprison Tahir, instead imposing a suspended six-month prison sentence, a 12-month supervision order, 150 hours of community service, a £80 victim surcharge, and a five-year ban from using the London Underground during rush hours. The incident was witnessed by undercover police officers.

A Californian man, Robin Barton, met the retired Santa Ana police officer, Michael Buelna, who saved his life by finding him abandoned as an infant in a dumpster 25 years ago. Barton was initially adopted by Elizabeth Barton and Daniel Fernandez, and both parties met Buelna last week. The reunion was significant as Buelna, who was also abandoned by his mother as a child, shares a bond with Barton. Despite his mother's past actions, Barton considers himself blessed with a loving family and expressed forgiveness. Buelna, who once wished to adopt Barton, now seeks to help Barton find his biological mother.

A 16-year-old student named Courtney Brain, who is a straight-A student with a near-perfect attendance record, was given a detention for missing half an hour of school due to an emergency GP appointment for a water infection. Her mother, Jane Burnham, criticized the school's decision to punish Courtney, claiming it was petty and unreasonable. The school argued that the detention was intended to give Courtney the best chance possible for her summer exams. Despite the school's stance, Mrs. Burnham does not believe the extra half-hour revision will significantly impact Courtney's grades, as she has already completed her coursework and practical work. The girl's attendance figure was contested by the school, which insisted it was 91.2 percent.

Graeme Finlay, a 53-year-old former naval serviceman, was cleared of beating up two elderly holidaymakers in a row over rudeness at dinner on a cruise ship. The incident took place on the Thomson Celebration luxury liner, where Finlay and the elderly couple, Ron Phillips (70) and June Phillips (69), were passengers. Finlay insisted he acted in self-defense when he was allegedly attacked by Mr. Phillips with a crutch. The jury at Teesside Crown Court returned unanimous not guilty verdicts in less than an hour on charges of unlawful wounding and inflicting grievous bodily harm. Following the verdict, Finlay expressed relief and stated that he regrets the events but is grateful for the jury's belief in his account.

An American transgender woman, Hayley Carney, aims to fulfill a lifelong dream by becoming a British citizen. She plans to move to the UK this year, marriage her online fiancée Anne, and then apply for a marriage visa to set her on the path to citizenship. Hayley has always found the UK more accepting of people like herself and has dreamed of living there since childhood. She is looking forward to starting a new life in England and becoming a British citizen.

Diego Simeone, the manager of Atletico Madrid, has expressed surprise at the absence of English clubs in the Champions League and Europa League, particularly after Chelsea, Arsenal, Manchester City, and Everton were eliminated in earlier rounds. In his column for goal.com, Simeone attributed the failure of English clubs to the enormous potential of English footballers and the league's financial power. Despite this, he believes that Spain is still home to the two best teams in Europe, with Real Madrid and Barcelona being among the last eight teams in Europe every season. Atletico Madrid will face Real Madrid in the second leg of their Champions League quarter-final on Wednesday, with the hosts missing key players like Karim Benzema, Gareth Bale, and Luka Modric due to injuries and suspensions.

David Cameron and Boris Johnson, known as the dream team, faced difficulty solving a children's jigsaw puzzle at a day nursery in Surbiton while promoting Tory plans for free childcare. The conservative duo encountered more errors than expected and attempted various solutions such as hammering pieces together and wedging them into place. After nearly nine minutes, they successfully completed the puzzle, and the pair shared a relieving group hug. They later moved on to a hand painting session with another group of children.

Justice Diana Bryant, a top judge in Brisbane, has advocated for a reformation of surrogacy laws in Australia to prevent instances of child abandonment. She suggests that commercial surrogacy should be legalized in Australia to regulate the practice ethically, addressing concerns raised by recent cases of abandoned children, such as the baby Gammy case. Bryant believes this change would ensure the biological parentage of children born through surrogacy can be known, particularly for those born overseas.

A six-month-old kitten named Seven, miraculously survived a seven-storey fall in Sydney, Australia, despite injuries including a broken jaw, broken leg, broken hard palate, and bruised lungs. The cat was found in a terrible state, covered in maggots and blood. The local vet clinic, My Vet Animal Hospital, shared the cat's story on social media, sparking widespread interest and donations to cover Seven's hefty medical bills. Although surgeries have already been performed, costing over $3000, Seven requires six more weeks of recovery before he is ready for a new home.

Simon Wood, a 38-year-old data manager from Oldham, was crowned the MasterChef champion in the series finale, showcasing a three-course meal that impressed judges John Torode and Gregg Wallace. Wood's victorious menu included octopus, squab pigeon, and lemon posset with various garnishes. His win concludes the eleventh series of the BBC cooking competition. Meanwhile, Kim Woodward, a former MasterChef semi-finalist, made history by becoming the first woman to be appointed head chef at the Savoy Grill in London, a position dating back to 1889. Woodward, who previously worked as a sous chef and later head chef at the York & Albany, is now leading a staff of about 35 chefs, including many women, at the prestigious five-star art deco restaurant.

1. Hull City manager Steve Bruce acknowledges the need for "crazy results" to secure Premier League survival, as the Tigers are currently two points above the relegation zone and have gone five games without a win.
2.Without a win in five games, Bruce's side face a difficult trip to Southampton this weekend, with goalkeeper Allan McGregor potentially under pressure due to recent errors.
3. In positive news for Hull, midfielder Tom Huddlestone is set to return from suspension and veteran goalkeeper Steve Harper is pushing for a starting spot, while Southampton are highly regarded by Bruce for their strong season.

Celebrity chef Bobby Flay, known for his work on the Food Network, is reportedly offering his ex-wife, Stephanie March, $5,000 a month from a prenup worth over $20 million. The prenup also includes a clause that allows him to buy their marital home for $1 million, with an additional $50,000 for moving expenses.

Stephanie March is expressed to be unhappy with the financial arrangement as she questions her husband's alleged past relationships, particularly with January Jones. The couple, who separated three weeks ago, is reportedly discussing the terms of their divorce.

Bobby Flay and Stephanie March's union is said to have faltered when Bobby did not immediately come to the hospital when Stephanie's appendix burst. This will be Stephanie's first divorce and Flay's third, who has a daughter from his second marriage. Prior to their separation, there were rumors of a potential romance between Flay and fellow chef Giada De Laurentiis.

Leading Australian modelling agencies are expanding their portfolios to include 'influencer' and 'blogger' divisions due to rising client demand for social media influence. This shift towards 'influencers' is in addition to the traditional beauty and fitness requirements. Models with high social media followings are now being prioritized, with an average expectation of clients ranging between 10,000 to 300,000 followers. This shift is driven by the potential for instant brand promotion and the desire for a 'cool girl' appeal. Notable models like Gigi Hadid and Mimi Elashiry, who have built their careers on social media, are now in high demand.

Hungarian architect Matyas Gutai and his collaborator Milan Berenyi have built a prototype house in Kecskemet, Hungary, using a novel liquid engineering system. The house, funded by the EU, features water-filled panels that equalize temperature across the building, allowing it to reheat itself and modify the indoor temperature with a monitoring system. This sustainable design, inspired by Gutai's visits to open-air hot baths, can produce its own energy, potentially reducing carbon emissions. Despite challenges related to cold weather and panel breakage, the system uses natural solvents to lower the freezing point of the water and incorporates special joint units for resilience. This innovative approach aims to use less energy, materials, and depend less on traditional energy suppliers, working towards a greener future in construction.

In the upcoming Championship game between Cardiff City and Leeds United, Cardiff City has decided to forgo their supporters' presence after returning their ticket allocation. This move is in support of a fan-led boycott due to a perceived lack of reciprocity in ticket allocations for the two teams. Leeds United has not yet confirmed the reason for the limited number of tickets offered to away fans, and have also rejected Cardiff's request for a 'beam back' of the game at the Cardiff City Stadium. The absence of Cardiff City fans at Elland Road will mark the first time in recent history that such a significant away following will be absent from a game between these two teams.

The Utah photographer Alan Lawrence initially harbored negative emotions upon learning his son Wil, who has Down Syndrome, but now views him as a source of light and inspiration. In a photo series titled 'Wil Can Fly', Lawrence portrays his son appearing to fly in various scenes, creating the illusion by holding him up and then cropping himself out. The photos, posted on his blog and Instagram, have received positive feedback, and Lawrence plans to donate half the proceeds from a calendar featuring the photos to two Down Syndrome foundations. Lawrence aims to raise awareness about Down Syndrome and hopes to photographed Wil flying in other destinations.

In February 2012, a stadium riot between supporters of Al-Masry and Al-Ahly football clubs in Egypt resulted in 74 deaths. This incident spurred further violent protests in Cairo, leading to another 16 deaths. Today, an appeals court upheld the death sentences of 11 fans from the case, with their final verdict being referred to the Grand Mufti. Many of the defendants are fans of Al-Masry, while nine police officers and three club officials are also among the 73 defendants. The football riots were the deadliest in Egypt's history, sparking bans on fans attending matches and leading to the suspension of the Egyptian league this year due to a stampede resulting in 22 deaths.

In the Ghanaian slum of Nima, a coding class for girls is organized every week in a local mosque by tech entrepreneur Regina Agyare, founder of Soronko Solutions. Her initial visit in 2014 was meant to be a one-off seminar as part of her mentorship initiative "Tech Needs Girls," but the girls proved engaging, prompting her to establish a regular coding club. The aims are to show the community the value of educating girls and provide female role models. Achievers Ghana, a non-profit organization supporting local girls, hosts the classes in a space provided by the mosque. The coding sessions are open to both boys and girls, with the goal to challenge traditional gender roles and empower girls to reach their full potential.

The St. Patrick's Parish in Stephensville, Wisconsin has canceled its 44-year tradition of mud-wrestling pigs in a summer fundraiser, following complaints that the animals were abused during the event. The parish announced that the Original Pig Rassle will be replaced this August with a human mud foosball tournament. Animal advocacy group Global Conservation Group launched an online petition against the event, which garnered over 81,000 signatures. The church has stated that it is moving in a different direction for its 45th annual Roundup and that its talents can be better spent in less controversial areas.

Maria Sharapova has withdrawn from Russia's Fed Cup semi-final against Germany due to a leg injury, a disappointment for the player who was looking forward to playing in her home city of Sochi where she grew up. Sharapova's last appearance was in the Miami Open at the end of March. Anastasia Myskina, the Russia Fed Cup captain, will now have to find a replacement for Sharapova. Meanwhile, Venus Williams has pulled out of the USA's World Group play-off against Italy due to personal reasons, with Lauren Davis set to take her place in the team led by Serena Williams.

A 36-year-old woman in police custody is suspected of posing as a Child Protective Services employee to lure and murder a young mother, Samantha Fleming, in Gary, Indiana. Fleming's body was found wrapped in plastic and doused with bleach on April 17. The suspect, who is in police custody at a Texas hospital for mental health reasons, is believed to have abducted Fleming's three-week-old daughter, Serenity. Incredibly, the infant was found safe with the suspect's sister and is expected to be returned to relatives in Anderson. The suspect had reportedly prepared a nursery in her house, leading investigators to believe she had long planned the crime.

An Ohio woman, La-Sonya Mitchell-Clark, discovered her biological mother, Francine Simmons, works at the same call-center operation company as she does and lives six minutes away after birth records were released by the Ohio Department of Health. Following their connection on Facebook, Mitchell-Clark learned she has three biological younger sisters, and the reunion has been a relief and amazing for the family. Simmons, who had Mitchell-Clark when she was 15, expressed shock at finding her daughter and happiness that they have finally connected.

An Icelandic duo has developed a new snack named the Jungle Bar, which uses cricket flour as one of its key ingredients. The bar, also containing dates, sesame seeds, and chocolate, is rich in protein and other essential nutrients. The duo hopes that the Jungle Bar, made by their company Crowbar Protein, will encourage Western consumers to consider incorporating insects into their diet. The product is currently being funded through a Kickstarter campaign. The duo has previously gained attention for their Fly Factory, a micro-factory that produces food using insect larvae.

A 73-year-old reserve deputy, Robert Charles Bates, accidentally shot and killed Eric Courtney Harris during an undercover operation in Tulsa, Oklahoma. The incident occurred while Bates was attempting to intervene using a less-lethal device, but he mistakenly discharged his service weapon instead of his stun gun. Harris was allegedly trying to sell a 9mm semi-automatic pistol and methamphetamine to undercover deputies when the shooting occurred. Bates, who has spent years working in law enforcement, is classified as an advanced deputy and has significant training in the use and identification of weapons.

A Russian unmanned spacecraft designated Progress 59, initially bound for the International Space Station (ISS), has lost contact with flight controllers and is expected to re-enter Earth's atmosphere between May 5 and May 7. The ISS and its six crew members are not at risk due to the significant difference in orbits. Despite the incident, Roscosmos is working on launching a new Progress resupply ship to the ISS in the third quarter of this year. The lost Progress spacecraft was carrying more than 3 tons of supplies, including food, fuel, and scientific equipment, but none of the supplies were critical for the US Operating Segment of the ISS, and no immediate risk to the ISS or its crew was detected.

Hull City manager Steve Bruce has announced that players will face salary cuts of up to 50% if the club is relegated from the Premier League. This measure aims to protect the club financially, as Hull currently has one of the lowest wage bills in the league. The Tigers are in 17th place and have a tough run-in to avoid relegation. Mo Diame, who has been out for five months with a knee injury, remains a doubt for the team's upcoming matches. In spite of their challenges, Bruce has praised the turnaround at Crystal Palace, specifically the work of Alan Pardew and Tony Pulis.

1. Restaurant critic and festival curator Leo Schofield, 79, expressed dissatisfaction with his decade-long stay in Tasmania, stating it was the unhappiest period of his life, causing close brushes with depression and suicidal thoughts.

2. Mr. Schofield moved to Tasmania to establish a Baroque music festival, but after facing funding cuts and disagreements with the government, he decided to relocate the festival to Brisbane.

3. Luke Martin, from the Tourism Industry Council of Tasmania, criticized Mr. Schofield's comments about Tasmania, describing them as 'blatant mistruths,' alleging that he asked for more funding and was upset when it wasn't granted.

The annual photography competition, held at the Northern Territory Cattlemen's Association's conference, invites participants to showcase the unique outback lifestyle, distinctive people, and landscapes of regional Australia. Marie Muldoon's heartwarming photo "True Love," a daughter cuddling a horse, won the overall competition and the People's Choice award in 2020. Previous winners include Jacynta Coffey in 2014, who won with "Trucking" and also took home awards for the People's Choice and NT Landscape categories for "Feeding the Bulls" and "Sunset Storm" respectively. The competition consistently highlights the relationship between people and animals in rural Australia, such as Tania Brooks' portrait "Noo Noo and Toby" from 2014.

The book "Sex by Numbers" explores various sexual myths and analyzes statistical claims about sexual behavior, including the average penis size, which a new study found to be around 5.2 inches in length and a 4.6 inch circumference when erect. The book also discusses myths about factors such as hand and foot size, exercise, pornography use, and baldness affecting sexual prowess, concluding that great sex is not necessarily dependent on penis size. Other interesting statistics covered include the average duration of sexual intercourse, which is nine minutes, the number of erections a man has per day, and the average quantity of semen ejaculated. The book sheds light on various misunderstandings about sexual behavior.

Barnet clinched promotion back to the Football League after a 2-0 victory over Gateshead in the Conference clash, with goals from Mauro Vilhete in the first and second half. This win secured the Conference title for Barnet, ensuring Martin Allen's fourth spell in charge would be his most successful. Gateshead played their part but were unable to mount a significant challenge. The play-offs will now determine Bristol Rovers, Grimsby Town, Eastleigh, and Forest Green Rovers' positions in the league, while Alfreton, Telford United, Dartford, and Nuneaton were relegated.

Remains of a missing college fresharian, Anjelica 'AJ' Hadsell, have been found in Franklin, Virginia, which is approximately 40 miles from her home in Norfolk. The discoveries were made on Thursday morning and the remains are undergoing identification and autopsy at the medical examiner's office. The investigation into Hadsell's disappearance, which has been ongoing since March 2, has now involve the FBI. There have been numerous hypotheses surrounding her disappearance, with AJ's family and friends expressing concerns about her being purposefully disappeared and a local twist coming with her stepfather's arrest for breaking into a home, claiming he was searching for his missing stepdaughter.

Apple is reportedly planning to use stronger materials, including 7000 series aluminum, to construct its next generation iPhone to prevent the 'bend gate' issue experienced by some owners of the iPhone 6 and iPhone 6 Plus. This material is currently used in the Apple Watch Sport and competition bicycles. The new iPhones, expected to be called the iPhone 6S and iPhone 6S Plus, are rumored to be unveiled in September and may include a A9 chip and Force Touch Feature. To avoid bending, users are advised not to have their phones sideways in a pocket, store them in a shirt pocket or bag, or use a case to maintain the phone's rigidity.

The article discusses the ongoing dominance of French and Irish teams in European rugby, with no English club winning the top prize since 2007. Bookmakers predict this trend to continue this year, with holders Toulon and Clermont being the favorites, followed by Racing and Leinster. English sides face tough challenges in the quarterfinals, with Bath, Northampton, Saracens, and Wasps all considered underdogs. English teams' struggles are attributed to less funding compared to their French counterparts, as well as the Irish system that rests top players for major European occasions. Nonetheless, there's optimism for an English team progressing, with Bath and Saracens being the top contenders.

A teacher named Sam Pearce, originally from Massachusetts, splits his time between teaching eighth-grade English in Brooklyn, New York, and modeling for high-end designers. He was discovered on the subway by another model, leading to a modeling contract with RED NYC. Despite juggling two demanding careers, Pearce maintains that both teaching and modeling require him to keep a straight face and feel that they are similar in their hectic nature. Recently, he launched a crowdfunding campaign to buy books for his students, seeing it as an opportunity to leverage his newfound fame for their benefit.

An amateur astronomer, Gordon Ewen, captured an unusual image of a sunspot that resembled a chick on the sun's surface. Sunspots are caused by concentrations of magnetic fields that reduce the surface temperature, making them stand out from the surrounding solar material. They can range significantly in size, with some being visible from Earth without a telescope. This photograph was taken using Ewen's telescope, which focuses on specific wavelengths of light, and he set up his observatory after retiring from his job five years ago. Sunspots have a temperature of 2,700 to 4,200°C and are the source of solar flares and coronal mass ejections, linked to magnetic fields. They should not be confused with coronal holes, regions of the corona where the magnetic field reaches out into space rather than looping back down onto the surface.

Vladimir Putin is reportedly planning to use the threat of nuclear war and potential acts of destabilization, such as cyber attacks or ethnic tensions, to maintain control of regions like Crimea and deter NATO from intervening. Notably, there are concerns about Russia's intentions towards the Baltic states, particularly Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania. The threat level is considered high enough that Lithuania has reinstated conscription. The story also mentions a new clothing line called The Army of Russia, which was unveiled at a fashion week in Moscow and features military-style clothing with pro-Russia slogans.

Virgin Galactic plans to test a new version of SpaceShipTwo by the end of the year, following the destruction of its previous spacecraft in a crash in 2014. The company aims to leverage lessons learned from that incident to improve the new spacecraft. Chief Executive George Whitesides stated that the new spacecraft is nearly ready and could begin test flights this year. The initial SpaceShipTwo was destroyed in a crash in the Mojave Desert, resulting in co-pilot Michael Alsbury's death and pilot Peter Siebold's injury.

In Cloverdale, east Perth, a refugee couple reported a racially motivated attack on their property by a neighbor, resulting in their children questioning their identity. Footage of the incident shows the neighbor brandishing a crowbar in a racially charged altercation that ended in a violent confrontation. The neighbor, who is a 51-year-old woman and a chef, has since been charged with assault, disorderly conduct, going armed in public, and conduct likely to racially harass after the footage went viral. However, the woman insists that she was the victim of the incident. The couple believes the woman's slurs have caused emotional distress, leading their children to question their ethnicity.

Walmart is under scrutiny after a theft at one of their stores in Tuscon, Arizona, where a thief, Mario Valencia, was able to shoot rounds from a rifle stolen from the store, despite the required gun locks. The stolen weapon was found to have a loose wire, allowing it to be fired immediately. A police chase ensued, and during the pursuit, Officer Michael Rapiejko utilized his vehicle to take down Valencia, who was later found to be involved in a crime spree involving theft, vandalism, burglary, home invasion, and car theft. Valencia is facing multiple felony charges, while Rapiejko was reinstated after being put on leave and cleared of any wrongdoing in the incident.

A Wisconsin father-of-five, identified as Peter Kelly, was stabbed to death at the St Croix River after an argument escalated with three other fishermen over noisy behavior. The incident occurred on the Wisconsin side of the river at around 9.45pm on Tuesday, resulting in Kelly's death at the scene. Authorities are still seeking the attackers, who were believed to be in their late teens or early 20s, along with their dog named Gunnar, and two vehicles with Minnesota license plates. The small community of St Croix Falls is mourning the loss of Kelly, who was a volunteer high school wrestling coach, husband to wife Christie, and a loving father to four boys and a girl all under the age of nine.

Holly Willoughby and Davina McCall have teamed up for the first time in a campaign for Garnier Nutrisse, where they show off their new hair colors and advocate for finding the perfect shade for UK women. Besides this, Holly has also launched a range of vintage-inspired baby clothes with BHS and is designing a home range for Sir Philip Green's high-street store. Meanwhile, Davina renewed her wedding vows with her husband Matthew Robertson in Las Vegas, and they have since embarked on a road trip around California.

1. A upcoming surge in funeral debts is expected due to the increase in deaths from the baby boom generation, which coincides with rising funeral costs in the UK.
2. According to a report by the International Longevity Centre-UK and backed by insurance firm OneFamily, the number of deaths in the UK will rise by 20% over the next two decades, impacting families financially and adding to the perceived financial strain on younger generations.
3. The cost of a 'simple' funeral, including a cremation, a minister, and an undertaker, has already risen by 80% over the past 10 years and is projected to continue rising, with additional costs for items such as memorial stones, death notices, and wakes, pushing the average cost of a full-service funeral to £5,423.

According to a TSA committee report released on Monday, full screening of airport employees nationwide would not significantly decrease overall public risk, as it cannot determine an individual's motivations or capabilities to cause harm. Instead, the report advocates for a risk-based, multi-layered security approach, which includes enhanced criminal background checks, screening of airport and airline employees when they travel as passengers, reducing access points to secure areas, and increased random screening of aviation employees. TSA Secretary Jeh Johnson announced immediate actions based on the report, and Sen. Charles Schumer praised it as a prompt response to closing security loopholes. The report also recommends strengthening employee vetting, expanding collection of domestic intelligence, and increasing surveillance of employees in baggage rooms and cargo areas.

Raheem Sterling, along with team-mate Jordon Ibe, was pictured smoking a shisha pipe earlier this season. Similarly, Arsenal midfielder Jack Wilshere has previously been involved in smoking-related controversies, including a cigarette in London, swimming pool in Las Vegas, and a shisha pipe in London. Other misbehaving stars, like Diego Maradona, Saido Berahino, Paul Merson, and Kyle Walker, have faced suspension, drug-related scandals, and poor judgment due to recreational substance use. Robin Friday, a former Reading forward, was known for his repute as a 'bad boy', due to drug-taking, drinking, womanizing, fighting, smoking, and wild behavior, despite his footballing talent. He retired at 25 and died 13 years later after a heart attack.

The article discusses an Ask Reddit thread where members of the disabled community share their frustrations about able-bodied individuals thinking they're being supportive but are actually offensive. Common pet peeves include being called an inspiration, being praised for doing ordinary activities like going to university, unsolicited help, and accusations of faking disabilities. Additionally, there's widespread disdain for advice on diets, remedies, or cures, and the topic of religion is often touchy. One user expresses their desire to be seen as a regular neighbor instead of an inspiration.

The article discusses an innovative car, EOssc2, developed by German engineers, designed to navigate and park in congested urban areas. Its unique features include the ability to turn on the spot, shrink in size, and move sideways like a crab. The goal is to create an 'ultra flexible micro-car for mega cities' that can form a train and save energy due to its semi-autonomous capabilities. The car is currently undergoing tests in Bremen, Germany, and Dalian, China.

Middlesbrough secured a 2-0 home victory against Rotherham United, with Lee Tomlin and Patrick Bamford scoring the goals. The second-half performance from Boro dominated the game, and despite a late penalty miss by Bamford, the team maintained their position in the fourth spot in the Sky Bet Championship table. The win came after a slow start and several close chances in the first half.

The Tewksbury Police Department in Massachusetts was infected with a form of malware called CryptoLocker, which encrypted vital records on their computer network. The department was forced to pay a $500 ransom in Bitcoin to regain access to their files, as the only uncorrupted files were 18 months old. This incident, reminiscent of past thefts from Swansea Police Department and Midlothian, Illinois police, highlighted the increasing threat of cybercrime in the U.S. police departments. It was emphasized that the attack did not constitute a data breach, as the information remained internal, but it was encrypted and made unreadable.

A Chinese woman, Zhu Diandian, has gained internet fame for her unique pet, a 187lb pig named Five Flowers, whom she treats as a family member and shares a bed with daily. Despite occasional jealousy from her pet dog, Zhu's husband is reportedly understanding of the situation. Zhu, whose surname sounds like 'pig' in Mandarin, has nicknamed her pet and posts photos of their bond on social media, sparking a wave of positive comments, including a Swiss follower considering to give up eating pork.

A diner, Louise Smith, secretly pulled two strands of hair from a young girl's head and planted them in her food at the Crown and Thistle pub in Cumbria last May. Despite ordering a £21 dinner, Smith was unable to pay and instead attempted to fraudulently get the meal for free by complaining about finding hairs in her food. CCTV footage from the pub showed Smith standing over the child and plucking hairs from her head. This week, Smith was convicted of fraud in her absence by Carlisle Magistrates' Court, and an arrest warrant has been issued for her as she is now on the run.

Thailand's Kiradech Aphibarnrat claimed victory in a play-off at the Shenzhen International, his second European Tour title, after teenager Li Hao-tong had looked poised for a home win with a closing 67 to finish 12 under par. Aphibarnrat, who had trailed by two shots with two holes to play, holed an 18-foot eagle putt on the 17th and just missed a birdie on the last, setting up a play-off. In the play-off, Aphibarnrat repeated his approach to the last and holed a birdie putt after Li missed from long range. Aphibarnrat had earlier struggled for form, having not won since 2013, and dedicated his win to his late coach and mother.

The article discusses two significant fights in boxing history: Floyd Mayweather vs Manny Pacquiao, predicted to be the most significant fight this century financially, and Joe Louis vs Max Schmeling, which occurred in 1938 and has political and cultural implications. A Liverpool couple, Linda and George Hunter, who spent years paying off their mortgage, find their home nearly worthless after a council scheme to sell neighboring homes for £1 turned their street into a 'ghetto'. The Hunters, who stayed put due to family ties, received an offer from the council to move to a similar house, but it fell through when their street became part of Liverpool's 'Home for a Pound' scheme. Celebrities such as Kim Kardashian, Mariah Carey, Myleene Klass, Amanda Holden, and Fearne Cotton celebrated Easter with their families by organizing egg hunts, baking treats, and preparing colorful Easter baskets. Gabrielle Yinka Saunders, a 32-year-old convicted fraudster, stole £17,000 from her second job at a City firm to fund her wedding and honeymoon. Despite having been convicted twice previously for fraud, Saunders was spared jail. A man named PJ Spraggins underwent a year-long fitness regimen to lose 70lbs to donate his kidney to his wife Tracy, who has Lupus and was on a seven-year long transplant waitlist. However, his blood pressure was initially too high for the operation. Undeterred, he continued his efforts and was eventually given the green light for surgery at Vanderbilt hospital in February 2015. The transplant was a success, and Tracy's kidney function is now at 100%. The couple is currently recovering at home in Birmingham, Alabama. A kind-hearted animal lover, Pauline Kidner, is nursing three abandoned badger cubs back to health. The cubs, one of which was rescued from a Jack Russell's mouth, are thriving on a diet that includes custard creams. The aim is to eventually release these badgers back into the wild once they're strong enough and ready for solids. However, if release isn't possible, they may need to be put down due to reduced human contact protocols.

Kimi Raikkonen, feeling optimistic about Ferrari's chances, believes the team can contend for the Formula One world title this year. In the Scottish Championship, Rangers manager Stuart McCall aims to address their recent poor away form on Saturday against Dumbarton.
